maps.title: CA26 · 4. VAT, excise duty and customs

nodeData.note: These are taxes on spending, not on income. Businesses collect them from customers and pass them to KRA. This topic shows how VAT works in Kenya, what excise duty is, and how tax is worked out on imported goods.

children.note: Start here: why spending taxes exist and who really pays them.
An indirect tax is charged on goods and services when people buy them. The seller collects it and pays it to the government, so the customer pays it without dealing with KRA.

manas.q: What is an indirect tax?

children.topic: The final customer carries the cost
children.note: Each business in the chain gets back the VAT it paid on its own purchases. Only the last buyer, the consumer, ends up bearing the tax.

children.topic: The business acts as tax collector
children.note: A VAT-registered duka or company adds VAT to its prices, keeps records, files returns and pays the money over. The VAT is not the business's income.
Income tax, PAYE and corporation tax are charged on what people and companies earn. VAT, excise and customs are charged on what is bought, made or imported.

VAT: the VAT Act 2013. Excise: the Excise Duty Act 2015. Customs: the East African Community Customs Management Act 2004, shared by EAC countries. Procedures and penalties: the Tax Procedures Act 2015.

manas.q: Which laws govern VAT, excise duty and customs in Kenya?

children.note: Spending taxes bring in steady money because people buy things every day. Excise is also used to discourage harmful goods such as alcohol and tobacco (link to Topic 1, public finance).
The core ideas: rates, output VAT, input VAT and what you pay KRA.
VAT is a tax on the value a business adds at each stage of making and selling something. Each business pays only on the part it added.

manas.q: What is value added tax (VAT)?

children.note: Most goods and services in Kenya carry VAT at 16% of the price before VAT. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the standard VAT rate in Kenya?

children.note: Zero-rated supplies (listed in the Second Schedule of the VAT Act) are taxable, but at 0%. The seller charges no VAT yet can still claim back the VAT on its purchases. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is a zero-rated supply?

children.topic: Exempt supplies: no VAT at all
children.note: Exempt supplies (First Schedule) are outside VAT. The seller charges no VAT and cannot claim back VAT on its purchases, so that VAT becomes a cost. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is an exempt supply and what happens to its input VAT?

children.topic: Output VAT: VAT on your sales
children.note: The VAT you charge customers on your taxable sales. You owe it to KRA.

manas.q: What is output VAT?

children.topic: Input VAT: VAT on your purchases
children.note: The VAT you paid suppliers on purchases used for your taxable business. You can deduct it from output VAT.

manas.q: What is input VAT?

children.note: Output VAT minus input VAT is what you pay KRA. If input is bigger, the extra is carried forward, or refunded in some cases.

manas.q: How is VAT payable worked out?

children.topic: Pulling VAT out of a price: 16/116
children.note: If a price already includes VAT at 16%, the VAT inside it is price × 16/116. Example: KES 11,600 × 16/116 = KES 1,600 VAT; price before VAT KES 10,000. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How do you find the VAT inside a VAT-inclusive price?

children.note: Who must register, how invoices work, and when and how to file and pay.
Who has to join the VAT system and who does not.
You must register if your taxable supplies are KES 5 million or more in a year. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the VAT registration threshold in Kenya?

children.note: A business below KES 5 million may ask to register, subject to KRA's conditions. It can then claim input VAT. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
A business that makes only exempt supplies does not need to register for VAT. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
A business may deregister if its taxable turnover falls below KES 5 million a year. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Non-resident suppliers selling through a digital marketplace must register for Kenyan VAT whatever their turnover. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

Turnover tax (1.5% of gross sales) is for residents with turnover above KES 1m and up to KES 25m. A TOT payer whose vatable supplies reach KES 5m must also register for VAT. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
The paperwork that proves the VAT.

VAT-registered persons must be on eTIMS. Tax invoices are serially numbered and generated from eTIMS; without one the buyer has weak support for an input claim. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: Where must a Kenyan VAT tax invoice be generated?

children.note: If a sale is reduced or goods are returned, issue a credit note within 6 months of the original invoice. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

children.topic: Tell KRA of changes in 21 days
children.note: Changes such as a new address or business details must be notified to KRA within 21 days. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Keep tax records in KES, in an official language, for 5 years from the end of the period they relate to (Tax Procedures Act s23). (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Deadlines and special rules.

children.topic: Tax point: when VAT becomes due
children.note: VAT is due at the earliest of: delivery or performance, a consultant's certificate, the invoice, or payment.

manas.q: What is the tax point for VAT?

children.note: File the VAT return on iTax and pay on or before the 20th of the following month. October VAT is due by 20 November. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: When are the Kenyan VAT return and payment due?

children.note: Make a payment slip on iTax, then pay at the bank or by M-PESA Paybill 572572 using the payment registration number as the account. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Input VAT can be claimed only within 6 months after the end of the period in which the supply was made. Later claims are lost. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How long do you have to claim input VAT in Kenya?

children.note: Extra input VAT is carried forward. A refund is possible only if it comes from zero-rated supplies, withholding VAT, or approved aid-funded supplies. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

Appointed withholding agents keep back 2% of the taxable value from the supplier and remit it to KRA by the 20th of the next month. The supplier treats it as a credit. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is withholding VAT?

children.note: If you buy a service from abroad, you charge yourself the VAT and pay it. You can claim it back as input VAT if the service is for your taxable business. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is reverse VAT?

children.note: KRA lists nil filers, non-filers and missing traders. Buyers cannot claim input VAT on invoices from traders on this list. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Two more taxes, often met together when goods are made or imported.
A tax on selected goods and services.
A tax on certain goods and services made in or imported into Kenya, listed in the First Schedule of the Excise Duty Act 2015. Examples include drinks, tobacco and packaged water.

manas.q: What is excise duty?

children.note: Some products are taxed per unit (per litre, per kilo) and some as a % of value. Check the First Schedule for the current amount; this map gives no product rates.
Makers and importers of excisable goods apply for an excise licence on iTax (Registration, other registration, Excise licence).
Many excisable goods must carry KRA excise stamps under the EGMS system, with a fee per stamp. Stamps help KRA spot fake or untaxed goods.
Excise returns are filed on iTax by the 20th of the following month. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Taxes collected at the border.
A tax on goods brought into the country (import duty). Duties and taxes on imports are paid before KRA releases the goods, unless exempt.

manas.q: What is customs (import) duty?

children.note: Kenya applies the EAC Customs Management Act 2004. Its Fifth Schedule gives exemptions, for example for returning residents' personal goods.
EAC members charge the same import duty bands on goods from outside the EAC. The rate depends on the goods' tariff code. Look up the current band; none is given here.

manas.q: What is the EAC Common External Tariff?

children.note: The value duty is charged on: usually the cost of the goods plus insurance and freight to Kenya (CIF), converted to KES.

manas.q: What is customs value?

children.note: First import duty on customs value. Then excise (if any) on value plus duty. Excise is part of the VAT base. Then VAT on value plus duty plus excise.

manas.q: In what order are import taxes calculated?

children.note: Use a licensed clearing agent. Typical documents: Import Declaration Form (IDF), customs entry, invoices, and a Certificate of Conformity for regulated goods. Declare on KRA's customs portal.
Imports may also carry other levies such as the IDF fee and Railway Development Levy. Their rates change, so check KRA before using them.
Real numbers in KES. Every answer is checked.
Buy for 10,000 + VAT 1,600. Sell for 12,000 + VAT 1,920. Pay KRA 1,920 − 1,600 = KES 320, the VAT on the 2,000 value you added. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
A Nairobi hardware shop, VAT registered, all sales standard-rated. October sales KES 2,500,000 and purchases KES 1,800,000, both before VAT.
2,500,000 × 16% = KES 400,000. Customers are billed KES 2,900,000. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
1,800,000 × 16% = KES 288,000, backed by valid eTIMS invoices. Suppliers are owed KES 2,088,000. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
400,000 − 288,000 = KES 112,000 VAT payable. File and pay on iTax by 20 November. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Dr Trade receivables 2,900,000 / Cr Sales 2,500,000 / Cr VAT control 400,000. Sales are recorded without VAT.
Dr Purchases 1,800,000 / Dr VAT control 288,000 / Cr Trade payables 2,088,000.
Dr VAT control 112,000 / Cr Bank 112,000.
Credits 400,000. Debits 288,000 + 112,000 = 400,000. Balance nil. A credit balance at month end shows VAT still owed to KRA.

manas.q: What does a credit balance on the VAT control account mean?

children.note: Three traders each buy inputs of KES 1,000,000 + VAT 160,000 and sell for KES 1,500,000 before any VAT.
Output 240,000 − input 160,000 = pays KRA 80,000. Cost stays 1,000,000; profit 500,000. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Output VAT nil. Input 160,000 claimed back (carried forward or refunded). Cost 1,000,000; profit 500,000. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
No output VAT and no input claim. The 160,000 becomes a cost: 1,160,000. Profit 1,500,000 − 1,160,000 = 340,000. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Zero-rating is better for the seller: input VAT comes back. Exemption hides VAT inside costs and prices, cutting profit by KES 160,000 here.
A Mombasa trader imports goods: CIF USD 20,000 at an illustrative KES 130 per USD. Duty and excise rates below are illustrative rates, not the real ones. Other levies are ignored.
Illustrative rate, not the real one: 25%. 2,600,000 × 25% = KES 650,000.
Illustrative rate, not the real one: 10% of value plus duty. (2,600,000 + 650,000) × 10% = KES 325,000.
VAT-registered importer claims the 572,000 as input VAT, so inventory cost is 3,575,000. Dr Inventory 3,575,000 / Dr VAT control 572,000 / Cr Payables & bank 4,147,000.

Late filing: 5% of tax or KES 10,000, the higher. On VAT of 400,000 that is 20,000. Paying 112,000 one month late: 5% (5,600) + 1% interest (1,120) = KES 6,720. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Where candidates and new bookkeepers lose marks or money.
Both charge no VAT on sales, but only zero-rated lets you claim input VAT. Always say which one it is.
If the price already includes VAT, use 16/116, not 16%. 16% of 11,600 is 1,856, which is wrong; the VAT is 1,600.

children.topic: Showing VAT as income or expense
children.note: For a registered business, VAT collected is owed to KRA and VAT paid is reclaimed. Neither goes to profit, except unclaimable input VAT.
Input VAT older than 6 months after the supply period cannot be claimed. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Input VAT on their invoices is blocked. Check suppliers before buying. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Import VAT is on customs value plus duty plus excise, not on the invoice price alone.
An agent that fails to withhold VAT faces a penalty of 10% of the tax involved. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Try each, then open the steps.
October taxable sales KES 800,000 before VAT. Purchases KES 580,000 including VAT. Find VAT payable.
A withholding agent receives an invoice of KES 232,000 including VAT. How much is withheld and paid to the supplier?
2% × 200,000 = KES 4,000, remitted to KRA by the 20th of next month. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
232,000 − 4,000 = KES 228,000. The supplier counts the 4,000 as a credit against its VAT.
Customs value KES 1,000,000. Duty at an illustrative rate, not the real one, of 10%. No excise. Find import VAT.
Wanjiru's salon has taxable supplies of KES 4.2 million a year. Must she register for VAT?

4.2 million is below KES 5 million, so she need not register. She may register voluntarily, subject to KRA conditions, or use turnover tax if eligible. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

Counttuts: the difference between VAT on sales and VAT on purchases.
The Chief Finance Officer: why zero-rated and exempt supplies differ.
KRATV: KRA's own short walk-through of filing a VAT return.
Edspira: what an excise tax is and why governments use it.
KRATV: a long KRA session on how small businesses import and clear goods.
Trusted pages for checking the rules.
KRA's official VAT page: rates, registration, returns, withholding VAT.
KRA's page on excise duty, licences and stamps.
KRA's steps and documents for importing goods.

maps.title: CA26 · 5. Tax procedures: returns, penalties, appeals

nodeData.note: How the tax system actually runs in Kenya: registering, keeping records, filing returns, paying on time, what happens when you are late, and how to argue with KRA. The main law is the Tax Procedures Act 2015 (TPA). It applies to the taxes you met in topics 2 to 4: PAYE, corporation tax, VAT and excise.

children.topic: What tax procedures are and why
children.note: The rules for HOW tax is collected, not how much. Topics 2-4 told you how to compute the tax; this topic tells you when to file, when to pay and what happens if you get it wrong.
The Tax Procedures Act 2015 (TPA) sets common rules for filing, paying, penalties, objections and refunds across income tax, VAT and excise. It is on Kenya Law.

manas.q: What does the Tax Procedures Act 2015 do?

children.topic: Who runs it: KRA and the Commissioner
children.note: Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) collects the tax. The Commissioner (KRA) makes assessments and decides objections and refund claims.
Most money lost to KRA by small firms is not the tax itself but penalties and interest for filing or paying late. Good procedures save real cash.
PAYE (topic 2), corporation tax (topic 3), VAT and excise (topic 4) each have their own return. This topic covers the deadlines and penalties for all of them.
Before you can file, you need a KRA PIN and you must keep proper records.
Your tax number on iTax. Every person and business dealing with KRA needs one. Misusing PIN rules is an offence: KES 2,000 per offence. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the penalty for a KRA PIN offence?

children.note: Add each tax you owe to your PIN: VAT when taxable supplies reach KES 5 million a year; an excise licence on iTax for excisable goods; turnover tax for small firms.
A VAT-registered business must tell KRA of changes (address, business details) within 21 days. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

TPA s23: keep records in an official language, in Kenya shillings, for 5 years from the end of the reporting period. Keep them longer if an amended assessment or case is still open. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How long must records be kept under TPA s23?

children.note: Sales and purchase invoices, eTIMS invoices, bank statements, payroll, and the books. A duka owner needs daily sales and purchase records even under turnover tax.
In Kenya you work out your own tax, file the return on iTax and pay it. KRA checks later. This is self-assessment.
The taxpayer computes and declares the tax due; KRA can review and change it later by an assessment.

manas.q: What is self-assessment?

children.note: VAT return and payment are due on or before the 20th of the following month, through iTax. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: When is the VAT return and payment due?

children.note: Excise returns are filed on iTax by the 20th of the following month. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
TOT return and payment by the 20th of the month after the tax period, via iTax or the M-Service App. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Withholding VAT agents remit what they withheld by the 20th of the following month. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
PAYE, income tax and rental income returns each have their own due date. Look them up on iTax before relying on a date from memory.
Generate a payment slip on iTax, then pay at the bank or by M-Pesa Paybill 572572 using the payment registration number as the account.
If you are registered for a tax and had no activity, you still file a nil return. Non-filers can land on the VAT Special Table, and buyers then cannot claim input VAT from them.

children.topic: Assessments: when KRA changes your tax
children.note: An assessment is KRA's official decision on how much tax you owe.
The return you file is treated as an assessment of your own tax.
TPA s29: if you do not file a return, KRA can estimate the tax itself and issue a default assessment.

manas.q: What is a default assessment (TPA s29)?

children.note: KRA can correct your self-assessment if it finds errors, for example missing sales.
An amended assessment must be made within 5 years. For fraud or wilful neglect there is no time limit. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the time limit for an amended assessment?

children.note: Records are kept 5 years (s23) because KRA can reopen a return for 5 years (s31(4)). Throw papers away early and you cannot defend yourself.
Being late costs you twice: a penalty for the late return and another for late payment, plus interest every month.
A fixed percentage of the tax due OR a minimum amount, whichever is HIGHER. The minimum is the floor. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How is a late filing penalty worked out?

children.note: 5% of the tax due or KES 10,000, whichever is higher. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the late filing penalty for VAT?

children.note: 25% of the tax due or KES 10,000, whichever is higher. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the late filing penalty for PAYE?

children.note: Companies and partnerships: 5% or KES 20,000. Individuals: 5% or KES 2,000. Whichever is higher. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: Late income tax return penalty: company vs individual?

children.note: KES 1,000 per month late, per the KRA turnover tax page. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
5% of the tax paid late. This is on top of any late filing penalty. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the late payment penalty under s83A?

children.note: 1% per month or part of a month on the unpaid tax. Two months and one day late counts as 3 months. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the late payment interest rate (s38)?

children.note: If you deliberately under-declare tax, the shortfall penalty is 75% of the shortfall. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
KES 1,000 per day, capped at KES 50,000. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Failing to deduct withholding VAT or withholding rental tax: 10% of the tax involved. Late payment of withholding taxes: 5%. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
You can apply to KRA for more time to pay or to pay in instalments. Ask before the due date.
An amnesty once waived penalties and interest if principal tax was paid by 31 Dec 2025. It has expired. Do not plan on it.
Real KES numbers. Check each one with a calculator.
VAT due KES 60,000. 5% = KES 3,000. The floor is KES 10,000, which is higher, so the penalty is KES 10,000. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
VAT due KES 400,000. 5% = KES 20,000, which is higher than KES 10,000, so the penalty is KES 20,000. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Tax KES 200,000 paid 3 months late. Penalty 5% = KES 10,000. Interest 1% x 3 months = KES 6,000. Extra cost KES 16,000; total paid KES 216,000. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
PAYE due KES 30,000. 25% = KES 7,500, below the KES 10,000 floor, so the penalty is KES 10,000. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
PAYE due KES 120,000. 25% = KES 30,000, above KES 10,000, so the penalty is KES 30,000. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Dr Tax penalties and interest (expense) KES 16,000 / Cr KRA payable KES 16,000. Penalties are a cost of being late, not part of the tax itself.
If you disagree with an assessment, follow the steps in order and never miss a deadline.
Object in writing within 30 days of the assessment notice. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How long do you have to object to an assessment?

children.note: It states the grounds, the undisputed tax is paid, and supporting documents are attached. Miss one and the clock may not even start.

manas.q: What makes an objection valid under s51?

children.note: KRA must decide within 60 days of a valid objection. If it does not, the objection is treated as allowed. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What happens if the Commissioner does not decide an objection in 60 days?

children.note: Appeal to the Tax Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of the objection decision (s51, s52). Undisputed tax must be paid or arranged. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
A party unhappy with the Tribunal can appeal to the High Court within 30 days. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
The last step under the TPA is the Court of Appeal, again within 30 days. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

children.topic: ADR: talk it out in 120 days
children.note: Alternative Dispute Resolution is voluntary mediation with a facilitator, not arbitration. It should finish in 120 days (s55). (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is KRA ADR and how long does it take?

children.note: Not for matters against the Constitution or law, pure technical points of law, cases needing a court ruling for the public, issues already decided by a court, or where a party is unwilling.
Object 30, KRA decides 60, Tribunal 30, High Court 30, Court of Appeal 30. ADR 120.

manas.q: List the dispute steps and their time limits.

children.note: If you paid too much tax, KRA can set it against other tax you owe (offset) or pay it back (refund).
An overpayment is usually used to clear other tax debts before any cash comes back.
Income tax: within 5 years. Other taxes: within 12 months. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: Time limits to claim an overpayment under s47?

children.note: The Commissioner should decide a refund claim within 120 days. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Excess input VAT is normally carried forward. A cash refund is possible only where it comes from zero-rated supplies, withholding, or approved aid-funded supplies.
Mistakes candidates make again and again.
Always compare the % with the minimum and take the HIGHER figure. 5% of KES 60,000 is not the answer; KES 10,000 is.
Late filing and late payment are separate penalties. Late return AND late payment means both apply, plus interest.
Interest is 1% per month or PART of a month. 2 months and 3 days = 3 months.
The PAYE late return penalty is much higher than VAT. Do not copy 5% across.
An objection that does not pay the undisputed tax is not valid, so the 60-day clock may not run.
The s37E amnesty ended with 31 Dec 2025. Do not give it as a current relief.
Try each one before opening the answer.
A trader files the VAT return late and pays KES 80,000 two months late. Total cost?
5% = KES 4,000; floor KES 10,000 is higher, so KES 10,000. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Penalty 5% = KES 4,000. Interest 1% x 2 = KES 1,600. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Income tax due KES 50,000, return late. Penalty for a company vs an individual?
5% = KES 2,500; floor KES 20,000 is higher, so KES 20,000. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
5% = KES 2,500; floor KES 2,000 is lower, so KES 2,500. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)
A valid objection is lodged and KRA has not replied after 60 days. What happens?
The objection is treated as allowed (s51). The taxpayer wins by default. (check the current KRA rule; checked 8 Nov 2026)

nodeData.note: A complex group is a family of companies where a subsidiary owns its own subsidiary, or where the parent owns a company both directly and through another subsidiary. This topic also covers what happens when the parent buys more shares, or sells some, over time.

children.note: Start here: who owns whom, and why the group still reports as one business.

children.topic: One family, one set of accounts
children.note: Group accounts show the parent and everything it controls as if they were a single business (a single economic entity). Inside trading is cancelled out.

manas.q: What does "single economic entity" mean in group accounts?

children.note: A company is consolidated when the parent controls it: power over the key activities, exposure to its returns, and the ability to use that power to affect those returns.

manas.q: Under IFRS 10, what three things make up control?

children.note: You already know goodwill, non-controlling interest (NCI), cancelling intra-group items and associates under IAS 28. Complex groups use the same tools, just with more layers.
The parent owns a subsidiary, and that subsidiary owns another company. The bottom company is a sub-subsidiary of the parent.

manas.q: What is a vertical (sub-subsidiary) group?

children.note: The parent owns some shares in a company directly AND more shares through one of its subsidiaries. Drawn on paper, the lines make a D shape.

manas.q: What is a mixed or D-shaped group?

children.note: Groups change: a parent may buy more shares in stages (step acquisition), or sell some or all of its shares (disposal). Each change has its own accounting rule.
Investors in the parent need to see the whole group. Wrong percentages or dates give the wrong goodwill, wrong NCI and a wrong profit figure.
Four IFRS standards work together for this topic. Learn what each one does in plain words.
Tells you when to consolidate (when you have control) and how to treat changes in ownership, including losing control.

manas.q: Which standard sets the control test and the rules on losing control?

children.note: Tells you how to account for the day you gain control: measure what you paid, the NCI and the net assets at fair value, and work out goodwill.

manas.q: Which standard covers goodwill on the date control is gained?

children.note: IAS 28 Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures covers significant influence (usually 20%–50%) and the equity method. Needed when an interest is an associate before or after a change.
IFRS 12 Disclosure of Interests in Other Entities asks the group to explain in the notes its subsidiaries, associates, NCI that matter, and the effect of changes in ownership.

manas.q: What does IFRS 12 deal with?

children.note: Smaller Kenyan groups may use IFRS for SMEs, which has simpler group rules. CPA Advanced exams use full IFRS.
How to handle a chain: H owns S, and S owns T.

children.topic: Is T a subsidiary of H?
children.note: Yes, if H controls S and S controls T. Control passes down the chain, even if H's effective share of T is below 50%.

manas.q: Can a sub-subsidiary be consolidated when the effective interest is under 50%?

children.note: Multiply the percentages down the chain. If H owns 80% of S and S owns 60% of T, H effectively owns 0.8 × 0.6 = 48% of T.

manas.q: How do you calculate the effective interest in a sub-subsidiary?

children.topic: NCI in T: direct plus indirect
children.note: NCI in T is everything H does not effectively own: 100% − 48% = 52%. That is 40% held by outsiders directly in T plus 12% held through S's own NCI (20% × 60%).

manas.q: How is NCI in a sub-subsidiary worked out?

children.note: Use the later of two dates: when H got control of S, or when S got control of T. T joins the group only once both links exist.

manas.q: What date is used to consolidate a sub-subsidiary?

children.topic: Cost of T from the group view
children.note: S paid for T, but H only owns 80% of S. So in T's goodwill working use only H's share of what S paid (80% of S's cost).

manas.q: What cost of investment is used in the sub-subsidiary goodwill working?

children.note: The other 20% of S's cost of T belongs to S's NCI. Deduct it from NCI so the investment is not counted twice.
Group retained earnings take H's 80% of S's post-acquisition profit and 48% of T's. The rest goes to NCI.
The parent holds the same company in two ways: directly and through a subsidiary.
H owns 60% of S and 25% of T. S owns 40% of T. H holds T both directly (25%) and through S.
H controls 25% of T's votes itself and 40% through S, which it controls: 65% in total. So T is a subsidiary.

manas.q: In a mixed group, how do you test whether the parent controls the bottom company?

children.note: Direct 25% plus indirect 60% × 40% = 24%, so H's effective interest in T is 49%. NCI in T is 51%.

manas.q: How is the effective interest in a mixed group calculated?

children.note: Cost of T for the group = H's direct cost plus H's 60% share of S's cost. Each purchase may have a different date and fair value, so check dates carefully.
Use voting control to decide IF T is consolidated. Use the effective interest to SPLIT T's profit between the group and NCI.
Buying shares in stages until you gain control.
The investor already holds some shares (often as an associate or a simple investment), then buys more and gains control. IFRS 3 calls this control achieved in stages.

manas.q: What is a step acquisition?

children.note: On the control date, revalue the shares you already held to fair value. Any gain or loss goes to profit or loss.

manas.q: In a step acquisition, what happens to the previously held interest?

children.topic: Rule 2: goodwill at control date only
children.note: Goodwill = what you paid now + fair value of the old holding + NCI − fair value of net assets, all measured on the day control is gained.

manas.q: What is the goodwill formula in a step acquisition?

children.note: While it was an associate, the old holding was equity-accounted under IAS 28. That carrying amount is what you compare with fair value.
Buying more shares in a company you already control is NOT a step acquisition. No new goodwill and no gain; it is a deal between owners in equity.
Selling shares: did the parent lose control or keep it?
This one question decides everything. Lost control: a gain or loss in profit or loss. Kept control: an equity transaction with no gain in profit or loss.

manas.q: What is the key question when a parent sells shares in a subsidiary?

children.note: Group gain = proceeds + fair value of any shares kept + NCI carrying amount − (net assets + goodwill) at disposal date.

manas.q: How is the group gain on losing control calculated?

children.note: If the parent keeps, say, 30%, that holding is remeasured to fair value and becomes an associate (IAS 28) or an investment from then on.
In H's own books the gain is simply proceeds minus the cost of the shares sold. The group gain is different because it uses net assets and goodwill.

manas.q: How is the gain on disposal worked out in the parent's own accounts?

children.note: Selling a small slice while still in control just moves value between owners. NCI goes up, and the difference to cash goes to equity, not profit or loss.

manas.q: How is a partial disposal that keeps control accounted for?

children.note: Buying more shares from the NCI is the mirror image: NCI goes down, cash goes out, and any difference is taken to equity.
In the year of a change, consolidate the subsidiary's income only up to the date control is lost (or from the date gained). Split profits by date.
Real numbers in KES millions (KES m). Every figure ties.
Nairobi-based H bought 80% of S on 1 Jan 2023 for KES 400m. S had bought 60% of T on 1 Jan 2022 for KES 200m. NCI is measured at its share of net assets.
H in S 80%, NCI in S 20%. H effective in T = 80% × 60% = 48%. NCI in T = 52%.
S controlled T from 2022, but H controlled S only from 1 Jan 2023. So T is consolidated from 1 Jan 2023.
Fair value of S's net assets: KES 420m (this includes its KES 200m investment in T). Fair value of T's net assets: KES 300m.

children.topic: Example 1: goodwill in S and T
children.note: Goodwill is worked at 1 Jan 2023 for both companies.
Cost 400 + NCI (20% × 420 = 84) − net assets 420 = KES 64m.
Group cost (80% × 200 = 160) + NCI (52% × 300 = 156) − net assets 300 = KES 16m.
64 + 16 = KES 80m on the group balance sheet.
At 31 Dec 2025 S has made KES 50m and T KES 100m since 1 Jan 2023.
84 − indirect holding adjustment (20% × 200 = 40) + 20% × 50 = KES 54m.
Net assets: H 700 (excl. investment) + S 270 (excl. investment) + T 400 + goodwill 80 = 1,450. Equity: share capital 500 + RE 688 + NCI 262 = 1,450.
H held 30% of A (an associate) carried at KES 90m. On 1 Jul 2025 H bought another 50% for KES 250m. The old 30% was worth KES 140m that day; A's net assets were KES 380m.
Fair value 140 − carrying amount 90 = KES 50m gain in profit or loss. Dr Investment in A 50 / Cr Profit or loss 50.
Paid 250 + old holding 140 + NCI (20% × 380 = 76) − net assets 380 = KES 86m.
H bought 80% of S for KES 300m when S's net assets were 300; NCI 60, goodwill 60. Later, with net assets of 400 and NCI of 80 (60 + 20% × 100), H sells the whole 80% for KES 450m.
Proceeds 450 + NCI 80 − (net assets 400 + goodwill 60) = KES 70m gain in group profit or loss.
Proceeds 450 − cost 300 = KES 150m. Different from the group's 70 because the group already counted S's profits and goodwill.
Sell 50% for 300; the kept 30% is worth 170. Gain = 300 + 170 + 80 − (400 + 60) = KES 90m. The 30% becomes an associate at 170.
H owns 90% of S and sells 10% for KES 70m. S's net assets are KES 500m; NCI is measured at share of net assets.
NCI rises by 10% × 500 = KES 50m.
Dr Cash 70 / Cr NCI 50 / Cr Equity (parent's reserves) 20. Nothing goes to profit or loss.
H owns 60% of S; NCI (40%) stands at KES 200m. H buys another 20% from NCI for KES 130m.
NCI falls by 20/40 × 200 = 100. Dr NCI 100 / Dr Equity 30 / Cr Cash 130. No new goodwill.
Where marks are usually lost.
For T in a chain, the group's share is the effective 48%, not the 60% that S holds. NCI in T is 52%, not 40%.
A sub-subsidiary bought before the parent bought S is consolidated from the date H got S, using T's fair values on that later date.
In T's goodwill use only 80% of S's cost. Forgetting this overstates goodwill and NCI.
Do not test control with the effective percentage. A 48% effective holding can still be a subsidiary because control flows down the chain.
A partial sale that keeps control never creates a gain in profit or loss. It goes to equity.
In a step acquisition, the old holding must be taken to fair value first, with the gain or loss in profit or loss.
Try each one, then open the steps.
H owns 75% of S and S owns 70% of T. What are H's effective interest and the NCI in T?
Effective interest = 75% × 70% = 52.5%.
NCI in T = 100% − 52.5% = 47.5%. T is still a subsidiary because control passes down the chain.
H gains control by buying more. The old 20% is now worth KES 60m. What is the gain?
60 − 45 = KES 15m gain in profit or loss; the 60 is used in the goodwill working.
Proceeds KES 90m; S's net assets KES 400m; NCI at share of net assets.
Still 65%, so control is kept: equity transaction.
NCI up by 15% × 400 = 60. Dr Cash 90 / Cr NCI 60 / Cr Equity 30.
Proceeds 200, net assets 150, goodwill 20, NCI 30. What is the group gain?
200 + 30 − (150 + 20) = KES 60m gain in group profit or loss.

nodeData.note: How to record deals done in another currency, and how to bring a foreign subsidiary into the group accounts. The rules come from IAS 21 The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates. This topic builds on Complex groups and the CA23 group accounts topics.

children.topic: What it is and why it matters
children.note: Kenyan businesses buy, sell and invest across borders. Exchange rates move every day, so the shilling value of a foreign deal keeps changing. IAS 21 tells you which rate to use and where the gain or loss goes.
The price of one currency in another, for example KES per US dollar. All rates in this map are made up for teaching, so each is marked 'illustrative rate'.

manas.q: What is an exchange rate?

children.note: The gain or loss that appears when the same foreign amount is turned into shillings at two different rates.

manas.q: What is an exchange difference under IAS 21?

children.note: Job 1: record a single company's foreign deals (transactions). Job 2: turn a whole foreign subsidiary's accounts into the group's currency (translation).

manas.q: What are the two main areas IAS 21 covers?

children.note: Listed companies and most groups use full IFRS, so IAS 21 applies. Smaller entities using IFRS for SMEs follow a similar section on foreign currency.
Before any translation, decide the company's own working currency and the currency the accounts are shown in.
The currency of the main economic setting where the business earns and spends its cash. A Nairobi shop selling and paying in shillings has KES as functional currency.

manas.q: What is functional currency?

children.note: Look first at which currency mainly sets selling prices and which currency mainly pays wages, materials and other costs. Then look at how it raises loans and keeps cash.

manas.q: What are the main clues for choosing a functional currency?

children.note: The currency the financial statements are shown in. A company may choose any presentation currency, for example a Kenyan group reporting in USD for investors.

manas.q: What is presentation currency?

children.note: Any currency other than the entity's functional currency. For a Mombasa importer with KES functional currency, USD is a foreign currency.
Only when the underlying business facts change. The change is applied from that date forward, not backwards.

manas.q: How is a change in functional currency applied?

children.note: Rules for a single company that buys or sells in a foreign currency.

children.topic: Day one: use the spot rate
children.note: Record the deal in your functional currency at the exchange rate on the day it happens (the spot rate). An average rate for a week or month is fine if rates do not move much.

manas.q: At what rate is a foreign currency transaction first recorded?

children.topic: Monetary items: money owed or held
children.note: Items that are cash or will be received or paid as a fixed number of currency units: cash, receivables, payables, loans.

manas.q: What is a monetary item?

children.note: Items with no right to a fixed amount of money: inventory, property, plant and equipment, prepaid rent, goodwill.

manas.q: Give examples of non-monetary items.

children.note: At the reporting date, restate monetary items at the closing rate. The difference goes to profit or loss.

manas.q: How are foreign monetary items treated at the year end?

children.note: Items at historical cost stay at the rate on the day they were bought. Items carried at fair value use the rate on the day fair value was measured.

manas.q: Which rate is used for non-monetary items?

children.note: How the exchange difference arises depends on whether the bill is paid before the year end.
Paid before year end. One exchange difference: the gap between the recorded amount and the cash actually paid. It goes to profit or loss.

manas.q: How is an exchange difference on a settled transaction treated?

children.note: Still owed at year end. Retranslate at the closing rate and take the difference to profit or loss now; a second difference arises when it is finally paid.

manas.q: How is an unsettled foreign payable treated at year end?

children.topic: When a currency cannot be exchanged
children.note: 2023 amendments (Lack of Exchangeability, for periods from 1 January 2025): if you cannot swap a currency in a normal market, estimate the rate an orderly deal would use, and explain it in the notes.

manas.q: What do the 2023 Lack of Exchangeability amendments to IAS 21 require?

children.note: To consolidate a subsidiary that keeps its books in another currency, first translate its statements into the group's presentation currency. This is the closing rate method.
Every asset and liability in the subsidiary's balance sheet uses the rate at the reporting date.

manas.q: Which rate translates a foreign subsidiary's assets and liabilities?

children.note: Strictly each item uses its own transaction-date rate. An average rate for the year is accepted as a close approximation if rates did not swing a lot.

manas.q: Which rate translates a foreign subsidiary's income and expenses?

children.note: Equity at acquisition (share capital and pre-acquisition reserves) stays at the rate on the acquisition date. Post-acquisition profits build up at the rates used each year.
Because different lines use different rates, a difference appears. It goes to other comprehensive income and builds up in a separate equity reserve.

manas.q: Where do translation differences on a foreign subsidiary go?

children.note: Goodwill and fair value adjustments on acquiring a foreign operation are treated as its assets. Keep them in the foreign currency and retranslate at the closing rate each year.

manas.q: How is goodwill on a foreign subsidiary treated under IAS 21?

children.note: If the group owns less than 100%, the non-controlling interest takes its share of the translation difference, just like profit.
On disposal, the translation reserve built up for that subsidiary moves from equity to profit or loss (reclassification) as part of the gain or loss on disposal.

manas.q: What happens to the translation reserve when a foreign subsidiary is sold?

children.topic: Loans that are part of the investment
children.note: If the parent lends to the subsidiary with no plan to be repaid, the loan is part of the net investment. In the group accounts its exchange differences go to OCI, not profit or loss.
Kenyan examples with made-up rates. Every rate here is an illustrative rate, not a real market rate.
A Mombasa importer (functional currency KES) buys goods for USD 10,000 on credit from a US supplier on 1 October. Year end is 31 December; payment is made on 15 February.
Illustrative rate KES 130/USD. USD 10,000 x 130 = KES 1,300,000. Dr Inventory KES 1,300,000 / Cr Trade payables KES 1,300,000.
Illustrative rate KES 132/USD. Payable now KES 1,320,000, up KES 20,000. Dr Exchange loss (P&L) KES 20,000 / Cr Trade payables KES 20,000. Inventory stays at KES 1,300,000.
Illustrative rate KES 128/USD. Cash paid KES 1,280,000. Dr Trade payables KES 1,320,000 / Cr Cash KES 1,280,000 / Cr Exchange gain (P&L) KES 40,000. Debits = credits = KES 1,320,000.
Illustrative rate KES 131/USD: cash KES 1,310,000. Dr Trade payables KES 1,300,000, Dr Exchange loss KES 10,000 / Cr Cash KES 1,310,000. Settled, so nothing to retranslate at year end.
Nairobi Holdings bought 100% of Kampala Ltd on 1 January when its net assets were share capital UGX 300m. Kampala keeps books in UGX. Rates are UGX per KES 1, all illustrative.
Illustrative rates, UGX per KES 1: 25 at acquisition (1 Jan), 27.5 average for the year, 30 at 31 December. More UGX per shilling means the UGX got weaker.
PPE 240m + inventory 90m + cash 96m = 426m, less payables 60m = net assets 366m. Equity: share capital 300m + profit for the year 66m = 366m.
At illustrative closing rate 30: PPE KES 8.0m, inventory 3.0m, cash 3.2m = 14.2m; payables 2.0m; net assets KES 12.2m.
Share capital at illustrative historical rate 25: UGX 300m / 25 = KES 12.0m. Profit at illustrative average rate 27.5: UGX 66m / 27.5 = KES 2.4m.
Net assets KES 12.2m less share capital 12.0m less profit 2.4m = translation reserve KES -2.2m (a loss, to OCI). Equity 12.0 + 2.4 - 2.2 = KES 12.2m, so it balances.
Opening net assets: 300/30 - 300/25 = 10.0 - 12.0 = -2.0m. Profit: 66/30 - 66/27.5 = 2.2 - 2.4 = -0.2m. Total KES -2.2m, matching the balancing figure.
Nairobi paid KES 13.2m. At illustrative rate 25: KES 13.2m x 25 = UGX 330m, less net assets UGX 300m = goodwill UGX 30m.
UGX 30m / 25 (illustrative rate) = KES 1.2m.
UGX 30m / 30 (illustrative closing rate) = KES 1.0m. Fall of KES 0.2m: Dr OCI (translation reserve) 0.2m / Cr Goodwill 0.2m.
KES 2.2m on net assets + KES 0.2m on goodwill = KES 2.4m in OCI. If Kampala is later sold, this KES 2.4m moves to profit or loss.
Places where students most often lose marks.
Only monetary items go to the closing rate in a single company. Inventory and equipment bought abroad stay at the historical rate.
For a foreign subsidiary, translation differences go to OCI, not profit or loss, until the subsidiary is sold.

children.topic: Goodwill left at the old rate
children.note: Goodwill on a foreign subsidiary must be retranslated at the closing rate every year; the change goes to the translation reserve.
Check how the rate is quoted. KES per USD: multiply USD by the rate. UGX per KES: divide UGX by the rate. Ask: should the shilling number be bigger or smaller?
Functional currency is a fact found from the business; presentation currency is a choice. Do not swap them.
When the group owns less than 100%, split the translation difference between the parent and the non-controlling interest.
Try each question, then open the bubbles for the steps. All rates are illustrative.
A Thika flower exporter (KES) sells to a UK buyer for GBP 20,000 on credit. Illustrative rate on sale KES 170/GBP; at year end KES 165/GBP. Show the entries.
20,000 x 170 = KES 3,400,000. Dr Trade receivables KES 3,400,000 / Cr Revenue KES 3,400,000.
20,000 x 165 = KES 3,300,000. Receivable falls KES 100,000. Dr Exchange loss (P&L) KES 100,000 / Cr Trade receivables KES 100,000.
A Ugandan subsidiary earns UGX 54m profit. Illustrative average rate UGX 27 per KES 1. What is the profit in KES?
Income and expenses use the average rate: UGX 54m / 27 = KES 2.0m.
A Kenyan subsidiary sells crude oil priced in USD, and most of its costs and loans are in USD. What is its functional currency?
USD. Sales prices and most costs are set in USD, so that is the main economic environment, even though the company is in Kenya.
A group sells a foreign subsidiary with a cumulative translation loss of KES 2.4m in equity. Where does it go?
Reclassify it from equity to profit or loss as part of the gain or loss on disposal: Dr P&L (disposal) KES 2.4m / Cr Translation reserve KES 2.4m.

children.note: Practical guides for bookkeepers, accountants and business owners.

nodeData.note: Practical guides for bookkeepers, accountants and business owners.

children.note: How individuals in Kenya get a KRA PIN, file the yearly return on iTax, pay any tax due and avoid penalties. Simple steps for employees, bookkeepers and small business owners.

eTIMS is KRA's free system for issuing electronic tax invoices. Almost every business in Kenya must use it, and since 2024 your business expenses only count for tax if backed by an eTIMS invoice (check the current KRA rule).
How to run a monthly payroll in Kenya: gross pay, NSSF, SHIF, housing levy and PAYE, the payslip, the journal, and paying and filing on time.
Practical Excel for people working in accounts: a clean sheet, the formulas you need daily, pivot tables, reconciliations, ageing debtors, a loan schedule and how to check your work.

How accounting programs keep the books for you: what they do, how they post double entry behind the scenes, how to choose and set one up for a small Kenyan business, and the routines and controls that keep the numbers right. Builds on At-work topics 2 (eTIMS invoicing) and 4 (Excel for accountants).

Month-end close is the short routine each month where you check, correct and lock the books, then hand the owner a clear report. This is At work topic 6, for people already keeping books in Kenya. It builds on Excel for accountants and Accounting software; next come M-Pesa reconciliation and Bookkeeping for a small business.
Checking that the M-Pesa money in your books agrees with the M-Pesa statement from Safaricom. Done often, it catches missing sales, charges, wrong payments and money taken out without a record.

Simple books for a duka, salon, matatu, pharmacy or small clinic. Keep business money apart, write a daily cash book, keep receipts, count stock, and do a short monthly profit and cash check so you know your profit and tax.

nodeData.note: How individuals in Kenya get a KRA PIN, file the yearly return on iTax, pay any tax due and avoid penalties. Simple steps for employees, bookkeepers and small business owners.

children.topic: What iTax is and why it matters
children.note: iTax is KRA's online system for registering, filing returns and paying tax. Almost every working adult in Kenya with a KRA PIN uses it at least once a year.
A KRA PIN is your personal tax number from the Kenya Revenue Authority. You need it for a job, a bank account, a business licence and to file returns.

manas.q: What is a KRA PIN?

children.note: You apply for a PIN online on iTax using your ID details. Once you have it, you keep the same PIN for life.
iTax is KRA's website for tax work: you log in with your PIN and password, file returns, generate payment slips and download certificates.

manas.q: What is iTax?

children.note: Filing on time keeps you free of penalties. A compliant tax record also helps when you need a tender, a loan or a Tax Compliance Certificate.
Filing a return means telling KRA your income and tax. Paying is a separate step. You can file on time and still owe a late payment penalty if you do not pay.

manas.q: Is filing a return the same as paying tax?

children.note: The basic rule is simple: if you have a KRA PIN, you file every year, even when you earned nothing.
Every individual with a KRA PIN must file an individual income tax return every year, even with no income (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Who must file an individual income tax return in Kenya?

children.note: Returns for a year of income can be filed from 1 January to 30 June of the next year (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When can you file your individual return for a year of income?

children.note: The deadline for the individual return is 30 June of the year after the year of income (check the current KRA rate). For 2025 income, that is 30 June 2026.

manas.q: What is the deadline for individual income tax returns?

children.note: The year of income for individuals is the calendar year, January to December. You file for last year's income in the first half of this year.
People who are exempt from tax must still file a return and enter their Exemption Certificate Number (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Do exempt persons need to file a return?

children.note: For persons with disability, the first KES 150,000 of monthly income is exempt (check the current KRA rate). They file using their Exemption Certificate Number.
Non-residents do not get personal relief (check the current KRA rate). Their tax works differently, so check with KRA or a tax adviser.
There are three common cases: employment income only, employment plus other income, and no income at all (NIL).
Most employees have only a salary. Your employer has already deducted PAYE every month, so the return mostly confirms those figures.
The P9 is your employer's tax deduction card for the year. It shows your pay and the tax deducted. Ask HR or payroll for it early.

manas.q: What is a P9 form?

children.note: Log in to iTax, choose the income tax return for residents, and enter or confirm your pay and tax from the P9. Then submit and save the receipt.
iTax may show your employer's figures already filled in. Check them against your P9 and payslips before you submit.
If you changed jobs, you need a P9 from each employer. Personal relief is claimed once, so you may end up owing a little tax.
If you also earn rent, business profit or side-hustle income, you must add it to the return and work out any extra tax.
Examples: profit from a duka, a matatu, consulting fees, or farm income. Each source is declared on the return.
Work out profit from your sales and expenses records. Guessing leads to errors that KRA can query later.
When other income is added, the total tax is often more than PAYE already paid. The difference is tax due, paid by the deadline.
A NIL return says you had no taxable income for the year. It is the quickest return to file.
File a NIL return if you have a PIN but earned no income in the year (check the current KRA rate). Students and the unemployed often need this.

manas.q: When do you file a NIL return?

children.note: NIL returns can be filed on iTax or on the KRA M-Service App (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Where can you file a NIL return?

children.note: If you had a salary, even for part of the year, a NIL return is wrong. File an employment return with your P9 instead.
An exempt person files the normal return and enters the Exemption Certificate Number given by KRA.
iTax gives an acknowledgement receipt. Save it as proof of filing. If tax is due, the next step is generating a payment slip.

children.topic: Reliefs and how tax is worked out
children.note: Your tax is worked out using tax bands, then reliefs are taken off. Knowing this helps you check your P9.
Annual bands: first 288,000 at 10%; next 100,000 at 25%; next 5,612,000 at 30%; next 3,600,000 at 32.5%; above 9,600,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the annual individual tax bands?

children.note: Monthly bands: first 24,000 at 10%; next 8,333 at 25%; next 467,667 at 30%; next 300,000 at 32.5%; above 800,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the monthly individual tax bands?

children.note: Personal relief is KES 28,800 a year, or 2,400 a month (check the current KRA rate). It is taken off the tax for resident individuals.

manas.q: How much is personal relief?

children.note: Insurance relief is 15% of premiums on life, education (10+ years) or health policies, up to KES 60,000 a year (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How is insurance relief worked out?

children.note: Tax payable = tax from the bands minus reliefs. Then subtract PAYE already deducted to see if you owe more or nothing.

manas.q: How do you get tax payable from tax on bands?

children.note: After filing, any tax due is paid using a payment slip from iTax.
On iTax, choose to make a payment, pick the tax and period, and generate the slip (check the current KRA rate). The slip shows the amount and a Payment Registration Number.

manas.q: What do you need from iTax before paying tax?

children.note: The PRN is the reference number on your payment slip. It links your money to your tax so KRA can credit your account.

manas.q: What is a PRN?

children.note: Use M-Pesa Paybill 222222 (the unified Government paybill). The account number is the PRN on the slip (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How do you pay KRA tax by M-Pesa?

children.note: Take the slip to an appointed KRA bank and pay over the counter (check the current KRA rate). Keep the bank receipt.
Save the M-Pesa message or bank receipt with the slip. They are your proof if iTax does not show the payment.
Late filing and late payment are charged separately. You can be charged both.
For individuals: the higher of 5% of the tax due or KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate). Even a NIL filer can be charged the KES 2,000.

manas.q: What is the late filing penalty for individuals?

children.note: If tax is paid after the due date: a penalty of 5% of the tax due (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the late payment penalty?

children.note: Interest of 1% per month is charged on unpaid tax until it is paid (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What interest does KRA charge on unpaid tax?

children.note: File by 30 June and pay by the same date. If you cannot pay in full, file anyway, so you avoid the late filing penalty.
Real numbers, step by step. Rates as confirmed on kra.go.ke today; always check the current KRA rate.
Mary earns KES 600,000 a year in salary. Let us work out her tax for the year.
117,400 − personal relief 28,800 = KES 88,600 tax for the year (check the current KRA rate).
If her P9 shows PAYE of 88,600, she owes nothing more. This is a simplified example that ignores other deductions.
Late filing penalty is the higher of 5% of tax due or KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate).
5% × 30,000 = 1,500. KES 2,000 is higher, so the penalty is KES 2,000.
5% × 100,000 = 5,000. That is higher than 2,000, so the penalty is KES 5,000.
Tax due is zero, so 5% is zero. The penalty is the minimum KES 2,000.
Otieno owes KES 60,000 on his duka profit. He files and pays 3 months after the deadline.
Higher of 5% × 60,000 = 3,000 or 2,000. Penalty = KES 3,000 (check the current KRA rate).
5% × 60,000 = KES 3,000 (check the current KRA rate).
1% × 60,000 × 3 months = KES 1,800 (check the current KRA rate).
60,000 + 3,000 + 3,000 + 1,800 = KES 67,800. Filing and paying on time would have saved KES 7,800.
Jane pays health and life premiums. See how the KES 60,000 cap works (check the current KRA rate).
15% × 48,000 = 7,200. Below 60,000, so her relief is KES 7,200 for the year.
15% × 500,000 = 75,000. That is above the cap, so relief is limited to KES 60,000.
Good records make filing quick and protect you if KRA asks questions.
P9 forms, payslips, filing receipts, payment slips, M-Pesa or bank receipts, insurance premium certificates and business sales and expense records.
For a duka or matatu, keep daily sales, receipts for expenses and bank or M-Pesa statements. These support the profit you declare.
Make one folder, paper or on your phone, for each year of income. File everything as it comes in.
Keep your PIN and password safe and private. Never share your password, even with a cyber café attendant.
These errors cause most penalties and KRA queries for ordinary filers.
People with no income think they need not file. They do, and a late NIL return can still cost KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Can you be penalised for a late NIL return?

children.note: Forgetting insurance relief on a qualifying policy means paying more tax than you should. Keep the premium certificate.
Typing pay or PAYE that differs from the P9 can show tax due that is not real, or trigger a query. Copy figures carefully.
If you were employed, a NIL return is wrong. You must declare your employment income.
iTax gets busy near the deadline. File early in the window so problems can be fixed in time.
Submitting the return does not pay the tax. Generate the slip and pay, or penalty and interest will build up.
Businesses have more filings. This map covers the individual return; others have their own maps.
A sole trader declares business profit on their own individual return, together with any salary.
A company has its own KRA PIN and files a separate corporate return. See the corporate tax map.
A business registered for VAT files VAT returns separately. See the VAT map.
An employer files PAYE returns for staff. This is the employer's job, not the employee's. See the PAYE map.
Try each one, then open the bubble for the answer steps.
Wanjiku got a PIN for a job application but earned nothing last year. What should she file?
A NIL return, on iTax or the KRA M-Service App, by 30 June (check the current KRA rate).
Compute the late filing penalty when the tax due is KES 50,000.
Compare with KES 2,000. The higher is 2,500, so the penalty is KES 2,500 (check the current KRA rate).
What paybill and account number do you use to pay KRA by M-Pesa?
Paybill 222222; the account number is the PRN on your iTax payment slip (check the current KRA rate).
Short videos from KRA's own channels. Screens may change, so follow what you see on iTax today.

nodeData.note: eTIMS is KRA's free system for issuing electronic tax invoices. Almost every business in Kenya must use it, and since 2024 your business expenses only count for tax if backed by an eTIMS invoice (check the current KRA rule).

children.topic: What eTIMS is and why it matters
children.note: Start here: what the system is, who must use it and why your expenses depend on it.
eTIMS stands for electronic Tax Invoice Management System. It is free KRA software that sends each invoice you make to KRA as you issue it.

manas.q: What does eTIMS stand for?

children.note: You can use eTIMS on a computer, a phone or a tablet, so even a small duka owner can invoice from a phone.

manas.q: On which devices can eTIMS be used?

children.note: All persons in business must onboard and issue electronic tax invoices, whether or not they are VAT-registered (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: Must a business that is not VAT-registered use eTIMS?

children.note: Companies, partnerships, sole proprietors, associations and trusts are all covered (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: Which types of business must onboard on eTIMS?

children.note: People paying Monthly Rental Income tax, Turnover Tax or annual income tax on business income must onboard (check the current KRA rule).
Small informal traders, like a mama mboga or a boda boda business, are also expected to onboard (check the current KRA rule).
Suppliers whose services are exempt from VAT, like a hospital giving medical care or a school, must still onboard (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: Must a VAT-exempt hospital or school onboard on eTIMS?

children.note: Since 1 January 2024 a business expense must be backed by an electronic tax invoice to be claimed for tax (check the current KRA rule). No eTIMS invoice usually means no deduction.

manas.q: From what date must a business expense be backed by an eTIMS invoice to be claimed?

children.note: KRA says eTIMS is free, runs on many devices, has a stock (inventory) module, keeps a record of all your invoices and makes filing returns simpler.

manas.q: Name four benefits of eTIMS that KRA lists.

children.note: KRA offers several ways (solutions) to use eTIMS. Pick the one that fits the size and setup of your business.
A web portal at etims.kra.go.ke where you log in and make invoices in the browser. Good for service businesses with few invoices.
Software you download for Windows or Android. It can handle several branches and tills, so it suits shops and pharmacies with many sales.
A simple web version reached through eCitizen. Handy for small traders who already use eCitizen.
Dial *222# on any phone to invoice. It is meant for individuals and sole proprietors, no smartphone or data needed.

manas.q: What is the eTIMS Lite USSD code, and who is it for?

children.note: An app from the Play Store or App Store for invoicing on a smartphone.
For businesses with their own invoicing or ERP system. The system is linked to KRA so invoices go to eTIMS automatically. VSCU and OSCU are the two integration types.

manas.q: Which eTIMS solution suits a business with its own invoicing system?

children.note: A special solution where the buyer, not the seller, makes the invoice. Covered in its own branch below.
You may register on more than one solution. Each has its own invoice number series, and all invoices show on your taxpayer portal (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: If you use two eTIMS solutions, do they share one invoice number series?

children.note: Onboarding means signing up your business on eTIMS. Steps differ a bit per solution; this is the general shape.
You need an active KRA PIN and your iTax login details before you start.
Decide which solution fits you: portal, Client, Lite (web, USSD or app) or system integration.
Register using your PIN on the chosen solution, e.g. on etims.kra.go.ke or eCitizen. Follow the on-screen steps.
KRA reviews the request; once approved you activate the solution and set up your device or till.
Load your products or services and regular customers so invoicing later is quick. The stock module can track goods.
Make your first real invoice and check that it appears on your taxpayer portal.
The daily work: making a sale invoice and correcting it with a credit note.
Your details, the buyer's PIN where they have one, the items, quantity, price and any VAT. eTIMS adds its own invoice number and sends it to KRA.
Business buyers need their PIN on your invoice so the expense counts for them. Always ask for it before you issue.
Log in, pick the customer, add items and quantities, check the VAT and total, then confirm. Print, share or send the invoice.
A credit note reduces or cancels an invoice already issued, for example when goods come back or a price was wrong.

manas.q: What is a credit note used for?

children.note: A credit note can only be raised from the same solution where the original invoice was made (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: From which eTIMS solution can a credit note be raised?

children.note: You cannot just erase a wrong invoice. You raise a credit note against it, then issue a correct new invoice.
Sometimes the seller is too small to invoice, so the buyer makes the invoice instead.
Where the seller is a small business or small-scale farmer with annual turnover not above KES 5 million, the buyer issues the invoice for them (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: When does the buyer issue the eTIMS invoice on the seller's behalf?

children.note: Buyer Initiated Invoicing is done through eCitizen (check the current KRA rule).
A Nakuru hotel buys KES 30,000 of sukuma from a small farmer. The hotel raises the invoice on eCitizen for the farmer, so the hotel's expense is backed.
Another option where the buyer generates the invoice instead of the seller. KRA offers it alongside BII in the same solution.

manas.q: What is reverse invoicing?

children.note: If you buy from small suppliers and nobody invoices, you lose the deduction. BII protects your own expense claim.

children.topic: Expenses that need no eTIMS invoice
children.note: Some costs are excluded from the eTIMS invoice rule (check the current KRA rule).
Staff pay is backed by payroll records, not an eTIMS invoice.
Imported goods have customs documents instead.
Airline tickets are excluded.
Capital allowances (investment deductions) are excluded.
Interest, and fees charged by financial institutions, are excluded.
Expenses already subject to final withholding tax are excluded.
Services from a non-resident with no permanent establishment in Kenya are excluded.
Remember: pay, imports, flights, investment allowances, interest and bank fees, final WHT, non-resident services.

manas.q: List the expenses excluded from needing an eTIMS invoice.

children.topic: Links to VAT and income tax
children.note: eTIMS invoices feed both your VAT return and your income tax computation.
The general VAT rate is 16% (check the current KRA rate). The old 8% rate on petroleum was deleted by the Finance Act 2023.

manas.q: What is Kenya's general VAT rate?

children.note: VAT charged on your sales invoices is output VAT, owed to KRA. eTIMS records it as you invoice.
VAT on your purchases is input VAT. Keep the supplier's eTIMS invoice as proof for any claim (check the current KRA rule).
Your eTIMS invoices are visible on the taxpayer portal, which makes filling the VAT return easier and helps match sales and purchases.
When working out taxable profit, an expense without a valid eTIMS invoice (and not excluded) is added back, so you pay more tax (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: What happens in the tax computation to an expense without a valid eTIMS invoice?

children.note: Before paying a supplier, check the invoice is a real eTIMS invoice with your PIN on it.
Wanjiku Supplies Ltd is VAT-registered. VAT is 16% (check the current KRA rate). Follow one sale, one credit note and one purchase.
Wanjiku sells goods for KES 50,000 plus VAT 8,000 (16%), total 58,000, and issues an eTIMS invoice.
Dr Receivables 58,000 / Cr Sales 50,000 / Cr VAT output 8,000. Debits 58,000 = credits 58,000.
The customer returns goods worth KES 10,000 before VAT. Wanjiku raises a credit note on the same eTIMS solution for 10,000 + VAT 1,600 = 11,600.
Dr Sales returns 10,000 / Dr VAT output 1,600 / Cr Receivables 11,600. Debits 11,600 = credits 11,600.
Wanjiku buys stationery for KES 20,000 + VAT 3,200 = 23,200. The supplier issues a valid eTIMS invoice with Wanjiku's PIN.
Dr Stationery expense 20,000 / Dr VAT input 3,200 / Cr Payables 23,200. Debits 23,200 = credits 23,200.
Output VAT 6,400 − input VAT 3,200 = KES 3,200 VAT payable to KRA.
If the stationery had no valid eTIMS invoice, the 20,000 is added back in the tax computation. Profit per books 40,000 − 20,000 = 20,000; taxable profit 40,000.
Errors that cost businesses money or cause trouble with KRA.

children.topic: Thinking only VAT payers need it
children.note: Wrong: all businesses must onboard, VAT-registered or not.
Paying a supplier on a handwritten receipt means the expense may not be deductible.
An invoice without the buyer's PIN does not help the buyer claim the cost.

children.topic: Credit note on the wrong solution
children.note: Trying to credit an invoice from a different solution fails. Use the solution where it was made.
Buying from small farmers without raising a buyer-initiated invoice loses the deduction.
Using an old rate or adding VAT to an exempt supply. Check the rate and item's VAT status.
Chasing an eTIMS invoice for salaries, bank charges or flights wastes time; these are excluded.
Try these, then open the steps.
Record a credit sale of KES 120,000 before VAT at 16%.
Dr Receivables 139,200 / Cr Sales 120,000 / Cr VAT output 19,200. Balances at 139,200.
A pharmacy pays KES 15,000 bank charges and KES 40,000 for cleaning with only a cash receipt. Which is deductible?
Fees of financial institutions are excluded from the rule, so the 15,000 can be claimed.
Cleaning needs an eTIMS invoice. With only a cash receipt, the 40,000 is added back.
A school buys maize from a farmer with turnover of KES 2 million. Who issues the invoice?
Turnover is not above KES 5 million, so the school (buyer) issues it through Buyer Initiated Invoicing on eCitizen (check the current KRA rule).
