nodeData.note: How to run a monthly payroll in Kenya: gross pay, NSSF, SHIF, housing levy and PAYE, the payslip, the journal, and paying and filing on time.

children.topic: What payroll is and why it matters
children.note: Payroll is the monthly job of working out what each worker earns, taking off the legal deductions, paying them and sending the deductions to the government bodies.
Pay staff the right net amount, and pass the deductions to KRA, NSSF and SHA on time.

manas.q: What is payroll, in one sentence?

children.note: The law makes the employer the tax collector for its staff. Money deducted belongs to KRA, NSSF or SHA, not to the business.
Any business with staff: a duka with two shop attendants, a matatu owner paying a driver, or a hospital with 200 nurses.
Topic 1 showed how to log in and file on KRA iTax. Payroll uses the same iTax account to file the monthly PAYE return.
Late or wrong deductions bring penalties and interest from KRA and the other bodies, and unhappy staff. Being on time is cheaper.
The same six steps happen every month. Follow them in order and payroll becomes routine.
Gather basic salaries, overtime, allowances, new joiners, leavers and advances before the cut-off date.
Add basic pay, allowances, overtime and taxable benefits to get gross pay for each worker.
Work out NSSF, SHIF, housing levy, then PAYE, then any other deductions like loans or SACCO savings.
A manager checks the payroll report, then net pay goes out by bank transfer or M-Pesa bulk payment.
Send PAYE and the other deductions to the right bodies and file the P10 PAYE return on iTax.
Post the payroll journal in the books, give payslips, and keep the records safe.
PAYE must be deducted, paid and the return filed by the 9th of the following month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: By when must PAYE be paid and the P10 return filed?

children.note: Gross pay is everything the worker earns before any deduction. It is the starting point for every calculation.
Basic salary plus allowances, overtime, commission, bonus and taxable benefits for the month.

manas.q: What is gross pay?

children.note: House, transport and lunch allowances paid in cash are part of gross pay and are taxed like salary.
Things given instead of cash, such as a company car, free housing or school fees paid for the worker.
Non-cash benefits become taxable when their total value is above KES 5,000 a month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When do non-cash benefits become taxable?

children.note: What the worker actually receives: gross pay minus all deductions.

manas.q: What is net pay?

children.note: Four deductions are set by law. Three come off before PAYE is worked out; PAYE is calculated last.
The National Social Security Fund saves for retirement. Worker and employer each pay 6% of pay (check the current KRA rate).
6% on pay up to the Lower Earnings Limit of KES 9,000, so at most KES 540 each side (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is NSSF Tier I (from Feb 2026)?

children.note: 6% on pay from KES 9,001 up to the Upper Earnings Limit of KES 108,000 (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is NSSF Tier II (from Feb 2026)?

children.note: Tier I and Tier II together cap at KES 6,480 for the worker and the same for the employer (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the maximum NSSF per side each month?

children.note: The employer pays the same amount as the worker on top of salary. It is a business cost, not a deduction.
The Social Health Insurance Fund, run by the Social Health Authority (SHA), funds health care.
2.75% of gross salary, with a minimum of KES 300 and no upper cap (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the SHIF rate?

children.note: SHIF is a contribution from the employee. The employer deducts it and sends it to SHA.
A levy that funds affordable housing. Both the worker and the employer pay.
1.5% of gross pay from the worker, plus a matching 1.5% from the employer (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the Affordable Housing Levy rate?

children.note: Remit within 9 working days after the end of the month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When must the housing levy be remitted?

children.note: Pay As You Earn is income tax taken from salary each month and paid to KRA.
First 24,000 at 10%; next 8,333 at 25%; next 467,667 at 30%; next 300,000 at 32.5%; above 800,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the monthly PAYE bands?

children.note: Every resident worker gets KES 2,400 a month taken off the tax (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How much is monthly personal relief?

children.note: 15% of qualifying insurance premiums, up to KES 60,000 a year, also reduces tax (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is insurance relief?

children.note: Housing levy, SHIF, registered pension/NSSF up to KES 30,000 a month and post-retirement medical fund up to KES 15,000 a month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Which items are deducted before PAYE is calculated?

children.note: Always calculate in the same order. Doing PAYE first is the most common beginner mistake.
Start with total gross pay for the month.
Work out the employee NSSF, SHIF and housing levy from gross pay.
Gross pay minus the allowed items (NSSF, SHIF, AHL) gives taxable pay.

manas.q: How do you get taxable pay?

children.note: Apply the PAYE bands to taxable pay, slice by slice, and add the slices.
Take off personal relief (and any insurance relief). The answer is PAYE, never below zero.
Gross pay minus NSSF, SHIF, AHL, PAYE and other deductions gives net pay.

manas.q: What is the net pay formula?

children.note: Two full payrolls in KES using today's rates (check the current KRA rate). Every figure is checked and the journals balance.
A hospital pharmacist earns KES 100,000 a month with no benefits.
NSSF 540 + 5,460 = 6,000; SHIF 2.75% = 2,750; AHL 1.5% = 1,500 (check the current KRA rate). Taxable pay = 100,000 - 10,250 = 89,750.
Salary 100,000 + employer NSSF 6,000 + employer AHL 1,500 = KES 107,500.

Dr Salaries 100,000; Dr Employer NSSF 6,000; Dr Employer AHL 1,500 / Cr PAYE payable 19,308.35; Cr NSSF payable 12,000; Cr SHIF payable 2,750; Cr AHL payable 3,000; Cr Net wages payable 70,441.65. Both sides 107,500.
A matatu driver earns KES 30,000 a month.
NSSF 540 + 1,260 (6% of 21,000) = 1,800; SHIF 825; AHL 450 (check the current KRA rate). Taxable pay = 30,000 - 3,075 = 26,925.
Salary 30,000 + employer NSSF 1,800 + employer AHL 450 = KES 32,250.

Dr Salaries 30,000; Dr Employer NSSF 1,800; Dr Employer AHL 450 / Cr PAYE payable 731.25; Cr NSSF payable 3,600; Cr SHIF payable 825; Cr AHL payable 900; Cr Net wages payable 26,193.75. Both sides 32,250.
Dr Net wages payable 70,441.65 / Cr Bank (or M-Pesa float) 70,441.65 when staff are paid.
Dr PAYE payable 19,308.35; Dr NSSF payable 12,000; Dr SHIF payable 2,750; Dr AHL payable 3,000 / Cr Bank 37,058.35.
After the numbers, the paperwork: a payslip for each worker, the journal in the books and the yearly records.
Name, month, gross pay item by item, each deduction, net pay and employer contributions. Give one every month.

manas.q: What should a payslip show?

children.note: Dr the expenses (salaries, employer NSSF, employer AHL); Cr each liability (PAYE, NSSF, SHIF, AHL) and net wages payable.

manas.q: What is the pattern of the payroll journal?

children.note: Deductions sit as current liabilities (money owed) until sent to KRA, NSSF or SHA.
The monthly PAYE return filed on iTax listing each worker's pay and PAYE. Due by the 9th of next month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the P10?

children.note: A yearly summary of a worker's pay and PAYE that the employer gives them, so they can file their own iTax return.

manas.q: What is the P9 form?

children.note: Keep payroll reports, payslips, P10 receipts and payment slips safely so you can answer any KRA question later.
These slips cause most payroll errors and lost exam marks.
Wrong: tax must be worked on taxable pay, after taking off NSSF, SHIF and AHL.
Every resident worker gets KES 2,400 a month off tax (check the current KRA rate). Missing it overstates PAYE.
Employer NSSF and AHL are extra business costs. Do not take them off the worker's pay.
A car or free house over the KES 5,000 limit must be added to gross pay (check the current KRA rate).
Rates change often. Old NHIF or old NSSF figures give wrong answers; always check the current rates.
Late PAYE brings penalties and interest. Diarise the deadline every month.
Check that total debits (gross + employer costs) equal total credits (all liabilities + net pay).
Try each one, then open the steps to check your answer.
Use today's rates (check the current KRA rate) and show each step.
NSSF 1,800 + SHIF 825 + AHL 450 = 3,075. Taxable pay 26,925.
Tax 3,131.25 less relief 2,400 = PAYE KES 731.25.
Salary 100,000 plus the employer's own contributions.

children.topic: Q3: Is a KES 4,000 benefit taxed?
children.note: A worker gets free lunches worth KES 4,000 a month.
No. Non-cash benefits are taxed only above KES 5,000 a month (check the current KRA rate).

children.topic: Q4: March PAYE is due when?
children.note: Think of the monthly deadline.
By 9 April: pay the PAYE and file the P10 on iTax (check the current KRA rate).

nodeData.note: Practical Excel for people working in accounts: a clean sheet, the formulas you need daily, pivot tables, reconciliations, ageing debtors, a loan schedule and how to check your work.

children.note: Most accounting jobs in Kenya use Excel every day, even where there is an accounting system. It is where you clean, check and explain the numbers.
A grid of cells where you type data and formulas, so the sheet does the sums for you and redoes them when the data changes.

manas.q: What is Excel, in one sentence?

children.note: Bank and M-Pesa reconciliations, debtor lists, sales summaries, budgets, loan schedules and reports for the boss.
iTax, eTIMS and payroll all give you downloads (CSV or Excel). This topic shows how to tidy and check those files.
Six March 2026 sales: Nairobi M-Pesa 12,500; Mombasa cash 8,200; Nairobi cash 4,300; Nairobi M-Pesa 7,750; Mombasa M-Pesa 15,000; Kisumu cash 6,250. Total KES 54,000.
A tidy layout makes every formula, filter and pivot table work first time. Messy sheets cause most errors.
Each row is one sale or one payment. Each column is one kind of detail: date, branch, payment, amount.

manas.q: What is the golden rule for laying out data?

children.note: Put short clear headings in row 1. No blank rows or columns inside the data, and no merged cells.
Keep rates and settings (like a commission rate) in their own labelled cells, not typed inside formulas.
Amounts must be real numbers, not text. Text numbers sit on the left of the cell and will not add up.
Click inside the data and press Ctrl+T. The Table grows when you add rows, and formulas copy down by themselves.

manas.q: How do you turn a range into an Excel Table, and why?

children.note: Give it a short name like Sales in Table Design. Then formulas read =SUM(Sales[Amount]) instead of =SUM(D2:D7).
A $ locks a cell so it does not move when you copy a formula. $F$1 stays $F$1 in every row.

manas.q: What does the $ do in $F$1?

children.note: Rate 5% sits in F1. In E2 type =D2*$F$1. For 12,500 the answer is 625. Copied down, Mombasa 8,200 gives 410.
Copied down all six rows, the commissions add up to KES 2,700, which is 5% of 54,000.
Click on the cell reference in the formula and press F4. Each press cycles $F$1, F$1, $F1, F1.
A small set of formulas does most accounting work. Learn these on the example sales data first.
Adds only the rows that meet every condition you give. Format: =SUMIFS(sum range, range1, rule1, range2, rule2).

manas.q: What does SUMIFS do?

children.note: =SUMIFS(D2:D7,B2:B7,"Nairobi",C2:C7,"M-Pesa") gives 20,250 (12,500 + 7,750).
Counts the rows that meet every condition. Same idea as SUMIFS but with no sum range.

manas.q: What does COUNTIFS do?

children.note: =COUNTIFS(C2:C7,"M-Pesa") gives 3.
Looks for an item in one column and returns the matching value from another. Format: =XLOOKUP(what, look in, return from, if not found).

manas.q: What does XLOOKUP do?

children.note: Codes P101 Paracetamol 120, P102 Amoxicillin 450, P103 ORS sachet 35. =XLOOKUP("P102",A2:A4,C2:C4,"Not found") gives 450.
=XLOOKUP("P109",A2:A4,C2:C4,"Not found") gives the words Not found instead of an error.
=VLOOKUP("P102",A2:C4,3,FALSE) also gives 450. The 3 means third column. Older Excel versions only have this one.

manas.q: Why must VLOOKUP end with FALSE?

children.note: FALSE asks for an exact match. Leaving it out lets Excel return a wrong nearby value without warning.
It only looks to the right, and the column number breaks if someone inserts a column. XLOOKUP has neither problem.

nodeData.note: How accounting programs keep the books for you: what they do, how they post double entry behind the scenes, how to choose and set one up for a small Kenyan business, and the routines and controls that keep the numbers right. Builds on At-work topics 2 (eTIMS invoicing) and 4 (Excel for accountants).

children.note: It is a program that records every money event once and then builds the ledgers, trial balance and reports for you. You enter documents; it does the bookkeeping.
Accounting software stores transactions and account balances on a computer instead of in paper books. Every report is drawn from the same stored entries.

manas.q: What is accounting software?

children.note: The chart of accounts is the numbered list of every account the business uses, grouped as assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses. Every entry must land in one of these accounts.

manas.q: What is a chart of accounts?

children.note: You raise an invoice to a customer, the software tracks what they owe and shows who is late paying (an aged receivables report).
You enter bills from suppliers, schedule payments and see what you owe and when (aged payables).
Bank or M-Pesa statement lines come into the program by a live feed or a file you import. You match each line to a record in the books so both agree.

manas.q: What does bank reconciliation in software mean?

children.note: Many packages count items in and out, so you know quantities on hand and the cost of goods sold without a stock card.
Some packages run payroll, others link to a separate payroll tool. Either way, the salary journal must reach the ledger. See At-work topic 3 (Running payroll in Kenya).

children.topic: Reports at the click of a button
children.note: Trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow, aged debtors and creditors and VAT summaries are produced from the same entries, for any date range.
You type one document; the software writes both sides of the entry for you. Knowing what it posts helps you spot mistakes.
Each invoice, bill, receipt or payment becomes a hidden journal with debits equal to credits. The software will not save an entry that does not balance.

manas.q: Why does accounting software always balance?

children.note: A credit sale posts Dr Receivables (customer owes you) / Cr Sales. When the customer pays: Dr Bank / Cr Receivables.

manas.q: What double entry does a credit sales invoice post?

children.note: A credit purchase of stock posts Dr Inventory (or Purchases) / Cr Payables. Paying the supplier posts Dr Payables / Cr Bank.

manas.q: What double entry does a supplier bill for stock post?

children.note: Receivables, payables and bank are filled only through invoices, bills and payments. Avoid manual journals into them, or the customer and supplier lists stop agreeing.
Click any figure in a report to see the entries behind it, down to the original invoice. This is how you trace an odd number.
Cloud software runs in a web browser and stores data on the vendor's servers; desktop software is installed on your own computer or office server.
You log in from a laptop or phone, the vendor runs updates and backups, and you usually pay a subscription. It needs a reliable internet connection.

manas.q: What is cloud accounting software?

children.note: The program and data sit on your machine or office server. It works offline, but you must do your own backups, updates and security.
Some desktop products can be hosted on a remote server or synced to the cloud, giving a middle path. Ask exactly where the data lives.
Think about power cuts, internet cost and reliability, whether staff work from more than one branch, and who will fix problems.

children.topic: Choosing for a small Kenyan business
children.note: List what you need first, then test two or three products against that list with a free trial or demo. Do not buy on adverts.

All persons in business must issue electronic tax invoices through KRA's eTIMS. Ask if the software connects to eTIMS by KRA's system-to-system option, or if you will invoice separately. Check the current KRA rule, 2 Nov 2026.

manas.q: What eTIMS question should you ask a software seller?

children.note: Can it take bank feeds or import M-Pesa and bank statements as files? Manual typing of every M-Pesa line is slow and error-prone.
If you buy or sell in USD or other currencies, check it can hold foreign currency accounts and work out exchange gains and losses.
Can you give each person their own login with limited rights, e.g. a cashier who can raise invoices but not see payroll?
Compare the full cost for three years: licences or subscription per user, add-ons, setup, training and support. Prices change, so get a written quote.
Is there a Kenyan partner or accountant who knows the product and can help when you are stuck at month end?
Ask how data is backed up, how you restore it, and whether you can export everything (to Excel or CSV) if you leave.
Customer and staff details are personal data under Kenya's Data Protection Act, 2019. Ask where data is stored and how it is protected.

manas.q: Which Kenyan law covers personal data held in accounting software?

children.note: Names you will meet in Kenyan offices. This list is not an endorsement and says nothing about features; check each on the maker's own site and in a demo.
Accounting products made by Intuit, in online and desktop editions. Check the current Kenyan offering and eTIMS position directly.
A cloud accounting product used by many small firms and their accountants worldwide. Check local support and eTIMS position.
A long-running family of accounting and payroll products in several editions. Ask a local partner which edition suits you.
Part of the wider Zoho family of business apps. Confirm features for Kenya in a demo.
A business-application suite where accounting is one module among others such as sales and stock. Usually set up by a partner.
Accounting software widely used by Indian-owned and trading businesses in East Africa. Check Kenyan tax setup with a partner.
A good setup saves months of clean-up. Get the accounts, tax codes and opening balances right before you enter daily work.
Enter the business name, KRA PIN, financial year end and base currency (KES). The year end decides when the software closes the year.
Start from the template, then add or rename accounts to fit the business. Keep it short; you can add detail later. Number accounts by type, e.g. 1000s assets.

manas.q: How should a chart of accounts be numbered?

children.note: Set tax codes so each sale or purchase line carries the right tax treatment. Ask your tax adviser for the current rates; do not guess. Check the current KRA rate.

manas.q: What is a tax code in accounting software?

children.note: On the start date, enter what the business owns and owes as one journal. It must balance; the gap is the owner's capital (equity).

manas.q: What is an opening balances journal?

children.note: Import lists of customers, suppliers and stock items with their opening unpaid invoices and quantities, so control accounts agree with the lists.
Run a trial balance on the start date and compare it line by line with the last Excel or paper balances before going live.

manas.q: What should you check before going live?

children.note: Two examples for Mama Wanjiku's general shop in Nairobi (a duka), which starts using software on 1 July. Figures in KES; the shop is not VAT-registered, to keep it simple.
What the shop owns and owes on 1 July, entered as one balancing journal.
Dr Cash in till 15,000; Dr M-Pesa till 35,000; Dr Bank 120,000; Dr Inventory 280,000; Dr Shop fittings 150,000; Dr Receivables 40,000. Total debits KES 640,000.
Cr Payables (suppliers) 90,000; Cr Bank loan 100,000. Total owed KES 190,000.
Capital = 640,000 − 190,000 = KES 450,000. Cr Owner's capital 450,000, so credits total 640,000 and equal the debits.
On 2 July a customer pays KES 2,000 by M-Pesa for goods that cost the shop KES 1,400.

children.topic: Entry 1: the money and the sale
children.note: Dr M-Pesa till 2,000 / Cr Sales 2,000. The software posts this when you save the cash sale receipt.
With stock tracking on, it also posts Dr Cost of sales 1,400 / Cr Inventory 1,400.
Software is only as good as the habit of feeding it. Small regular jobs beat a big panic at month end.
Record sales, receipts and M-Pesa takings; issue eTIMS invoices; file paper or photo copies of documents against each entry.
Import or refresh bank and M-Pesa lines and match them; chase overdue customers from the aged receivables list; enter supplier bills.
Reconcile every bank and M-Pesa account to the statement, run payroll, check the trial balance, review profit and loss, then lock the month.

manas.q: What are the main month-end tasks in accounting software?

children.note: For each statement line, find or create the matching entry. Any line left unmatched is a missing or wrong entry to fix.

manas.q: What does an unmatched bank statement line tell you?

children.note: Since 1 January 2024 an expense needs an electronic tax invoice to be claimed for tax. Attach it to the bill in the software. Check the current KRA rule, 2 Nov 2026.

manas.q: Since when must a business expense be backed by an eTIMS invoice?

children.note: If you buy from a small seller or farmer with turnover up to KES 5 million a year, you as buyer raise the invoice on eCitizen for them. Check the current KRA rule, 2 Nov 2026.

manas.q: What is Buyer Initiated Invoicing under eTIMS?

children.note: Controls stop honest mistakes and make fraud harder. Most are settings you switch on once.
Give each person their own login and only the rights their job needs. Never share one admin password.

manas.q: Why give each user a separate login and role?

children.note: A log of who entered, changed or deleted what and when. Review it monthly and keep it switched on.

manas.q: What is an audit trail?

children.note: After a month is reconciled and reported, set a lock date so no one can post into it by accident.

manas.q: What does a lock date do?

children.note: Keep regular backups or exports in a second place. Try a restore now and then; an untested backup may not work.
Where staff allow, the person who records payments should not also approve and pay them.
Plan the move like a small project. See At-work topic 4 (Excel for accountants) for cleaning the data first.
Start at the beginning of a month or year, so opening balances come from a closed, reconciled period.
Remove duplicate customers and suppliers, fix names and PINs, and use the software's import template columns.
For the first month, keep Excel too and compare totals. Stop once they agree.
Show each user only the screens they need. Write a one-page how-to for daily jobs.
Traps that cause wrong reports or tax problems.

children.topic: Opening balances that do not balance
children.note: Forcing the gap into a 'suspense' or 'opening balance adjustment' account hides an error. Find the missing figure instead.
Everything ends up in one account and the profit and loss tells you nothing. Use clear expense accounts.

children.topic: Journals straight into bank or debtors
children.note: Manual journals into control accounts break reconciliation and customer statements. Use receipts and payments.
Deleting a posted invoice loses the history. Issue a credit note or reversing entry so the trail stays.
Unmatched lines pile up and become impossible to trace. Reconcile every month.
One lost laptop or one ex-employee can wipe out years of records.
Short questions like those a manager or examiner may ask. Try them before opening the answers.
A salon starts software with Bank 60,000, equipment 90,000, stock 25,000 and suppliers owed 15,000. What is capital?

children.topic: Step 2: take off what it owes

children.note: A shop enters a supplier bill for stock of KES 48,000 on credit, then pays it from the bank. What does the software post?
Dr Inventory 48,000 / Cr Payables 48,000.
Dr Payables 48,000 / Cr Bank 48,000. Payables is back to nil for this bill.
The M-Pesa statement shows a KES 230 transaction charge with nothing in the books. How do you fix it?
Create a spend money entry from the reconciliation screen: Dr Bank charges 230 / Cr M-Pesa till 230.
Match the new entry to the statement line. Books and statement now agree.

nodeData.note: Month-end close is the short routine each month where you check, correct and lock the books, then hand the owner a clear report. This is At work topic 6, for people already keeping books in Kenya. It builds on Excel for accountants and Accounting software; next come M-Pesa reconciliation and Bookkeeping for a small business.

children.note: First understand what closing the month means and what you get out of it.
A fixed set of checks and adjustments done after the last day of the month, so the books show the true position for that month. When it is done, the period is locked and reports are issued.

manas.q: What is a month-end close?

children.note: Owners make decisions on these numbers: restocking the pharmacy, hiring, paying suppliers. Errors found monthly are small and easy to fix; errors found at year-end are big and costly.

children.topic: Accrual basis: match costs to months
children.note: Record income when earned and costs when used up, not only when cash moves. That is why the close adds accruals, prepayments and depreciation.

manas.q: What does the accrual basis mean for month-end?

children.topic: The goal: a clean trial balance
children.note: Every account checked and explained, debits equal credits, and nothing left in suspense. From that clean trial balance you build the management accounts pack.
Year-end adds audit, tax computation and full financial statements. A good monthly close makes year-end a thirteenth easy month instead of a crisis.
In this map we follow a small clinic with a pharmacy in Nairobi. It sells for cash, card and M-Pesa, buys drugs on credit, and has staff on payroll.
Start with the easy, hard-evidence items: is everything in the right month, and does cash agree?
Make sure each sale, purchase and expense sits in the month it belongs to. A delivery received on 31 October is an October cost even if the invoice comes on 3 November.

manas.q: What is cut-off at month-end?

children.note: Look at the last delivery notes and the first invoices of the new month. Check stock received and goods dispatched near the date match the right month's books.
Gather bank statements, M-Pesa till and paybill statements, supplier statements, payroll report, petty cash vouchers and the stock count sheets. Missing papers are the main cause of a slow close.
Match the cash book to the bank statement and list the differences: uncleared cheques, deposits in transit, bank charges not yet booked. Book the charges, then the balances should agree.

manas.q: What does a bank reconciliation do?

children.note: Match the M-Pesa till or paybill statement to sales recorded in the system, and record M-Pesa charges. The next map, M-Pesa reconciliation, covers this step by step.
Count the cash in the box with a second person present. Cash plus signed vouchers should equal the fixed float; record the vouchers as expenses and top up the float.

manas.q: How do you check petty cash at month-end?

children.note: Now agree each ledger to its control account and post the month-end adjustments.
The list of what each patient or insurer owes (debtors ledger) must add up to the receivables control account in the general ledger. Investigate any difference before moving on.

manas.q: What must the receivables ledger agree to?

children.note: The total of all supplier balances (creditors ledger) must equal the payables control account. Also match big suppliers to their own statements.
Tick your ledger against the supplier's statement. Differences are usually invoices in transit, payments not yet received by them, or credit notes missing.
A cost you have used this month but have not yet been billed for, such as electricity or water. Book it as an expense now and a liability (accruals).

manas.q: What is an accrual?

children.note: A cost you paid in advance, such as three months' rent. Keep the unused part as an asset (prepayments) and move one month into expense each month.

manas.q: What is a prepayment?

children.note: Spread the cost of equipment, furniture and vehicles over their useful lives. Most software runs it from the fixed asset register; check new purchases and disposals are in the register first.

manas.q: What is the monthly depreciation run?

children.note: Count stock on hand (fully or for high-value lines) and compare to the system quantity. Book the shortage as stock loss and look into the cause.

manas.q: What do you do when the stock count is less than the books?

children.note: Post gross pay as salaries expense, and the deductions and net pay as liabilities until they are paid. Check the payroll report totals agree to the journal.

manas.q: What does the payroll journal record?

children.note: Suspense holds items you could not place yet, like an unknown M-Pesa receipt. Find out what each one is and move it to the right account, so suspense ends the month at zero.

manas.q: What should the suspense account show after the close?

children.note: Monthly tax and payroll items are filed and paid through KRA iTax. Rates and deadlines change, so check the current KRA deadlines and rates on kra.go.ke.
Income tax deducted from staff pay. It is declared on KRA iTax and remitted monthly; agree the return to the payroll report.

manas.q: Where is PAYE filed in Kenya?

children.note: Payroll deductions for health insurance (SHIF), pensions (NSSF) and the Affordable Housing Levy. They are remitted monthly; check the current KRA deadlines and rates on kra.go.ke.
If the business is VAT-registered, the VAT return is filed monthly on iTax. Agree output VAT to sales and input VAT to valid purchase invoices before filing.

manas.q: How often is the VAT return filed?

children.note: Sales invoices go through KRA's electronic tax invoice system (eTIMS). Agree the eTIMS total for the month to sales in your books and explain any gap.

manas.q: What do you match eTIMS invoices against?

children.topic: Keep proof of filing and payment
children.note: Save each iTax acknowledgement and payment slip in the month's close folder. It saves hours when KRA or the auditor asks.
This map gives no rates or due dates on purpose, because they change. Always check the current KRA deadlines and rates on kra.go.ke.
With the adjustments posted, review the numbers and turn them into a report people can use.
Scan every line: is the balance on the side you expect, is it close to last month, can you explain it? A cash account in credit or negative stock means something is wrong.

manas.q: What do you look for in a trial balance review?

children.note: A short monthly report for the owner or board. It usually holds a profit and loss, balance sheet, cash summary and a few key numbers (KPIs).

manas.q: What is in a management accounts pack?

children.note: Income and costs for the month and the year to date, side by side with budget.
What the business owns (assets), owes (liabilities) and the owner's stake (equity) on the last day of the month.
Opening cash, money in, money out, closing cash, plus a short look ahead at big payments coming.
A few numbers the owner watches: gross margin, debtor days, stock days, cash in hand. Keep them the same every month so trends show.

manas.q: Name four useful KPIs for a clinic pharmacy.

children.note: Compare each actual line to budget and explain the big gaps in one plain sentence. Example: electricity KES 18,500 vs budget KES 15,000, KES 3,500 adverse (23.3%) because of a new X-ray machine.

manas.q: What is a variance review?

children.note: After sign-off, close the month in the accounting software so nobody can post to it by mistake. Later fixes go into the next open month with a clear note.

manas.q: Why do you lock the period after closing?

children.topic: Close calendar and who does what
children.note: A simple five-working-day timetable keeps everyone on track.

manas.q: What is a close calendar?

children.note: Stop posting old-month items late, collect statements and count sheets, count petty cash.
Bank and M-Pesa reconciliations, receivables and payables agreed to control accounts, supplier statements checked.
Post accruals, prepayments, depreciation, stock adjustment and the payroll journal. Clear suspense.
Prepare PAYE, SHIF, NSSF, Housing Levy and VAT figures, match eTIMS to sales, review the trial balance.
Issue the management pack with variance notes, get sign-off, lock the period.
Collects documents, does reconciliations and posts routine entries.
Posts adjustments, prepares tax figures, reviews the trial balance and writes the pack.
Reads the pack, asks questions, approves payments and signs off the month.
Someone other than the preparer checks each reconciliation and initials it. Two pairs of eyes catch most errors.
Clinic in Nairobi, October 2026. Every entry balances and the trial balance agrees before and after.
October power is used, but the bill only comes mid-November. Estimate from the meter reading: KES 18,500.
Dr Electricity expense KES 18,500 / Cr Accruals KES 18,500. October now carries its own power cost.
Reverse it on 1 November: Dr Accruals 18,500 / Cr Electricity 18,500. When the real bill is posted, only the difference hits November.
On 1 October the clinic paid KES 270,000 rent for October to December.
Dr Prepayments KES 270,000 / Cr Bank KES 270,000. It is an asset because two-thirds is still to be used.
KES 270,000 / 3 = KES 90,000 a month. Dr Rent expense 90,000 / Cr Prepayments 90,000. KES 180,000 stays as prepayments at 31 October.
Lab equipment cost KES 1,200,000, useful life 5 years, no value at the end, straight-line method.
Dr Depreciation expense KES 20,000 / Cr Accumulated depreciation KES 20,000. The asset's cost stays the same; its book value falls.
System stock at cost KES 640,000. The pharmacy count on 31 October finds KES 625,500.
640,000 − 625,500 = KES 14,500 missing (expired, damaged or lost).
Dr Stock loss (cost of sales) KES 14,500 / Cr Inventory KES 14,500. Then find out why: expiry, theft or dispensing errors.
Dr: bank 350,000; receivables 180,000; inventory 640,000; prepayments 270,000; equipment 1,200,000; cost of sales 420,000; salaries 260,000. Total KES 3,320,000.
Cr: accumulated depreciation 240,000; payables 210,000; capital 1,820,000; sales 1,050,000. Total KES 3,320,000, so it balances.
Electricity 18,500, rent 90,000, depreciation 20,000, stock loss 14,500. Total new expense KES 143,000.

Dr: bank 350,000; receivables 180,000; inventory 625,500; prepayments 180,000; equipment 1,200,000; cost of sales 420,000; salaries 260,000; electricity 18,500; rent 90,000; depreciation 20,000; stock loss 14,500. Total KES 3,358,500.
Cr: accumulated depreciation 260,000; payables 210,000; accruals 18,500; capital 1,820,000; sales 1,050,000. Total KES 3,358,500, so it still balances.
Before: 1,050,000 − 420,000 − 260,000 = KES 370,000. After: 370,000 − 143,000 = KES 227,000. Without the close, profit was overstated by KES 143,000.

nodeData.note: Checking that the M-Pesa money in your books agrees with the M-Pesa statement from Safaricom. Done often, it catches missing sales, charges, wrong payments and money taken out without a record.

children.topic: What it is and why it matters
children.note: Your till or Paybill holds real business money, so treat it like a bank account and check it like one.
M-Pesa is a mobile money service launched in Kenya in 2007 by Vodafone and Safaricom. Businesses take payments with Lipa na M-Pesa (Till or Paybill).

manas.q: When and by whom was M-Pesa launched?

children.note: Comparing two records of the same money and explaining every difference until both agree. Here: your books against the M-Pesa statement.

manas.q: What does reconciliation mean in accounting?

children.topic: Till = a bank account in the books
children.note: Open a ledger account called 'M-Pesa Till' (a cash/bank-type asset). Money in is a debit, money out is a credit, just like the bank account.

manas.q: How is an M-Pesa till treated in the books?

children.note: Without a check you can miss sales, pay for charges you never booked, or not notice money taken out. Your profit and your cash figure would both be wrong.
The bookkeeper, or in a small duka, pharmacy or clinic the owner. Ideally someone who does not also handle the till money.
Daily for busy tills, at least monthly as part of month-end close. Small daily checks are much easier than one big monthly hunt.

children.topic: Till, Paybill and the key words
children.note: Know the parts of your M-Pesa business account before you start matching.
Customers pay to a till number shown at the counter. Good for shops, pharmacies and clinics selling over the counter.
Customers pay to a business number plus an account number (e.g. invoice or patient number). Helps you see who paid for what.
Safaricom's business terms: the head office or store number groups your tills; the till number is what customers see.

manas.q: What is the difference between a store number and a till number?

children.note: The phone number authorised to withdraw money from the store. Safaricom says the till notification SIM cannot be the nominated number.

manas.q: What is the nominated number on an M-Pesa Business Till?

children.note: A way to receive business money on a personal line. Easy to start, but business and personal money get mixed, which makes reconciling harder.
Safaricom lists USSD *234# and the M-PESA Business App for managing the till and getting statements.
Your M-Pesa statement is the outside record you check your books against.
Safaricom says merchants can get daily, monthly or yearly statements on demand after opting in, also through the Business App.

manas.q: How does a merchant get M-Pesa till statements?

children.note: A typical statement shows a unique code for each transaction (letters and numbers). This is your best matching key.

manas.q: What is the best field to match M-Pesa transactions on?

children.note: When the money moved. Helps match a sale on your POS at 10:42 to the payment at 10:42.
Usually who paid or where money went, e.g. a customer name or a transfer to bank. Helps explain odd lines.
Money in and money out in separate columns. Charges usually appear as their own withdrawn lines.
The balance after each line. The closing balance is the figure you reconcile to.
The routine: get both lists, tick what agrees, then explain what does not.
Download the statement for the period. Print or export your cash book (M-Pesa ledger), POS sales report and any invoices paid by M-Pesa.
Last period's reconciled balance should be this period's starting point. If not, fix the old period first.
Match each statement line to a book entry by code, amount and date. Tick both sides.
Anything left on the statement but not in the books, or in the books but not on the statement, is a difference to explain.
Items that are on the statement but missing from the books (charges, unrecorded sales, withdrawals) need entries in the cash book.
Show the adjusted cash book balance equals the statement balance after timing items. Sign and date it.
Most differences fall into a few familiar groups.
Customer paid but the sale was not entered in the POS or cash book. Add it to the books.

manas.q: A customer paid on the till but the sale was not recorded. Which balance do you adjust?

children.note: Charges taken by Safaricom show on the statement. Use the charge shown on the statement; never guess an amount.

manas.q: How do you treat M-Pesa transaction charges found on the statement?

children.note: Money moved from till to bank. If booked on one date but showing on the statement on another, it is a timing difference.

manas.q: What is a timing difference?

children.note: Someone paid your till by mistake. The money is not yours: record it as owed back, not as a sale, and return it.

manas.q: How do you record money paid to your till by mistake?

children.note: Safaricom may reverse a payment a customer made in error, after contacting you for permission. Remove that sale from the books.
Owner pays school fees or shopping from the till. This is drawings, not a business expense.

manas.q: How is the owner's personal spending from the till recorded?

children.note: Typing mistakes, e.g. 4,700 entered as 7,400 (swapped digits). The difference of 2,700 divides by 9, a classic sign.

manas.q: What clue suggests a transposition error?

children.note: A short table that proves your books and the statement agree.
Part 1 adjusts the cash book for items you did not know about. Part 2 adjusts the statement for timing items. Both must end at the same figure.

manas.q: What are the two parts of a reconciliation statement?

children.note: Charges, unrecorded receipts, owner withdrawals, reversals, wrong-till money and your own errors. These need journal entries.
Timing items only, e.g. a bank transfer you booked today that shows on the statement tomorrow. No journal needed.

manas.q: Which items adjust the statement rather than the cash book?

children.note: Adjusted cash book balance = adjusted statement balance. If not, keep looking; never plug the gap.

manas.q: What must be true when a reconciliation is finished?

children.note: A Nairobi pharmacy reconciles its till at 31 October. All charge figures are illustrative, not real Safaricom tariffs.
Cash book (M-Pesa Till ledger) shows KES 184,600 debit. The statement closing balance is KES 199,360. The difference is 14,760.
Charges KES 1,240 (illustrative); customer sale not in POS KES 3,500; KES 2,000 paid to our till by mistake; owner withdrawal KES 5,000; reversal of a double payment KES 1,800.
A sale of KES 4,700 entered as 7,400 (overstated by 2,700). A KES 20,000 transfer to bank booked on 31 Oct shows on the statement on 1 Nov.
199,360 − 20,000 transfer not yet on statement = KES 179,360. Both agree, so the reconciliation is done.
Each cash book adjustment gets an entry so the ledger is right. Debits equal credits in every one.
Dr M-Pesa charges (expense) KES 1,240 / Cr M-Pesa Till KES 1,240.
Dr M-Pesa Till KES 3,500 / Cr Sales KES 3,500.
Dr M-Pesa Till KES 2,000 / Cr Payable – wrong-till payment KES 2,000. When returned: Dr Payable 2,000 / Cr M-Pesa Till 2,000.
Dr Drawings KES 5,000 / Cr M-Pesa Till KES 5,000.
Dr Sales KES 2,700 / Cr M-Pesa Till KES 2,700, bringing the sale down from 7,400 to 4,700.
Dr Sales KES 1,800 / Cr M-Pesa Till KES 1,800, removing the duplicate payment that was refunded.
Simple habits that make reconciling quick and stop losses.
Match today's till to today's POS before closing. Small gaps are easy to explain the same day.
The person who withdraws from the till should not be the one who reconciles it. One checks the other.

manas.q: Why separate till withdrawal from reconciliation?

children.note: Keep business money off personal lines. Pochi or a personal number mixes things and hides drawings.
Only a trusted person should hold the number that can withdraw. Review who has it.
Get regular statements so you always have the outside record to check against.

children.topic: Return money that is not yours
children.note: Safaricom encourages merchants to reverse money that does not belong to them. Keep a note of each case.
File each signed reconciliation with the statement. Auditors and KRA queries are easier with a paper trail.
A spreadsheet speeds up matching when there are hundreds of payments.

children.topic: Put both lists side by side
children.note: Statement on one sheet, POS or cash book on another, each with a column for the transaction code.
=XLOOKUP(A2,Books!B:B,Books!C:C,"MISSING") brings the book amount next to each statement line. Rows showing MISSING need checking.

manas.q: Which Excel function finds statement codes missing from the books?

children.note: =IFERROR(VLOOKUP(A2,Books!B:C,2,FALSE),"MISSING"). Use FALSE for exact match or results will be wrong.

manas.q: Why use FALSE in VLOOKUP for reconciliation?

children.note: Add a column: statement amount minus book amount. Anything not zero is an error to fix.
Run the lookup from the books to the statement to find entries that never reached M-Pesa.
Filter 'MISSING' rows and sum them. Those totals feed your reconciliation statement.
Watch for these when reconciling or answering exam questions.
Charges and unrecorded sales change the cash book, not the statement. Only timing items adjust the statement.
It inflates sales and profit. It is a liability until you return it.
Owner's personal spending is drawings. Putting it in expenses understates profit and tax.
Record sales at the full amount and charges as an expense, so both are visible.
Never post an unknown difference to make it balance. Find it, or record it as a clearly named suspense item and follow up.
Try each one, then open the steps.
Charges 300 not booked; customer receipt 2,000 not booked; transfer to bank 10,000 booked, not on statement. Prove they agree.

children.topic: Q2: Owner paid rent at home from till
children.note: KES 8,000 from the business till paid the owner's house rent. Give the entry.
Dr Drawings KES 8,000 / Cr M-Pesa Till KES 8,000. It is not business rent expense.

nodeData.note: Simple books for a duka, salon, matatu, pharmacy or small clinic. Keep business money apart, write a daily cash book, keep receipts, count stock, and do a short monthly profit and cash check so you know your profit and tax.

children.note: Books are simple written records of the money coming in and going out of your business. They answer four questions: am I making a profit, where is my cash, what tax do I owe, and can I show a lender my numbers?
Writing down every sale, every payment and every amount owed, on the day it happens, so nothing is lost or forgotten.

manas.q: What is bookkeeping?

children.topic: Know if you make a profit
children.note: A busy shop is not always a profitable shop. Only your records show whether sales are bigger than all your costs.
Books tell you how much should be in the till, on M-Pesa and in the bank today, so you can spot losses quickly.
KRA works out tax from your sales or profit. Without records you guess, and a guess can mean paying too much or paying penalties.

children.topic: Get a loan or SACCO credit
children.note: Banks and SACCOs ask for sales records, bank and M-Pesa statements before they lend. Clean books make the answer easier.
Records show your best-selling items, slow months and rising costs, so you can stock and price better.
Treat the business as separate from you, even if you own it alone. Mixing money is the most common reason small businesses cannot tell if they are making money.
In the books the business is one "person" and the owner is another. The business owes you what you put in and records what you take out.

manas.q: What does the business entity idea mean for a small business owner?

children.topic: Own till, M-Pesa line and bank account
children.note: Use a separate till number or business M-Pesa line and a separate bank account for the business. Do not run shop money through your personal phone.
Cash or stock the owner takes for personal use, like school fees or food for home. It reduces what the business owes you; it is NOT a business expense.

manas.q: What are owner's drawings?

children.note: Decide a weekly or monthly amount to take and record it every time. Taking cash "when needed" makes the books impossible to follow.

children.topic: Stock you take home counts too
children.note: If you take sugar or soap home from the duka, write it down as drawings at what it cost you.
Money the owner puts into the business, like savings used to buy first stock. Record it as capital, not as sales.

manas.q: What is capital in a small business?

children.note: A few simple books, kept every day, are enough for most small businesses. You can use an exercise book, Excel or accounting software (see the Excel and Accounting software maps).
One page per day: opening cash, money received, money paid out, and closing cash. It is the heart of small-business books.
Date, details, receipt or invoice number, money in, money out, and a running balance. Add columns for cash, M-Pesa and bank if you use all three.
Opening cash + money received − money paid = closing cash. Count the till at night; the count should match this figure.

manas.q: What is the cash book balancing rule?

children.note: Fill it in before closing the shop. Memory fails by the weekend, and small amounts disappear.
If the count differs from the book, write the difference as "cash short" or "cash over" and find out why. Never quietly adjust the figures.
Every payment needs a paper or electronic proof. File them by month in an envelope or folder, or photograph them the same day.
Receipts, invoices, M-Pesa messages and bank slips are the proof behind every line in your books.

manas.q: What is a source document?

children.note: An eTIMS invoice is a tax invoice made through KRA's system. Ask suppliers for one; it proves your purchase to KRA (see the eTIMS invoicing map).
Use a receipt book with printed numbers so a missing receipt is easy to spot.
A small fixed cash float kept apart from the till for tiny costs like boda fares, milk or photocopies.
A fixed float amount, for example KES 5,000. Spend from it with a voucher for each payment, then top it back up to the same amount.

manas.q: What is the imprest system?

children.note: A small slip saying date, what was bought, amount and who took the money. Staple the receipt to it.
At top-up time cash left + vouchers must equal the float. You refill only the total of the vouchers.
Treat your till number or business M-Pesa line like a second cash box with its own column and balance.

children.topic: M-Pesa column in the cash book
children.note: Record each M-Pesa sale and payment with the transaction code. Charges and withdrawal fees are business costs.
Each week download the M-Pesa and bank statements and tick every line against your book (see the M-Pesa reconciliation map).

manas.q: Why compare your books with the M-Pesa statement?

children.note: Taking till cash to the bank is not a cost or a sale. Show it as money out of cash and money into bank.

children.topic: Who owes whom, and your stock
children.note: Many small businesses sell on credit and buy on credit. Keep simple lists so no money is forgotten, and count stock so you know your real profit.
A page per customer, or one list, showing what they took, when, and what they have paid. Also called accounts receivable.

manas.q: Who are debtors?

children.note: A list of suppliers you owe, with invoice numbers and due dates, so you pay on time and are not charged twice. Also called accounts payable.

manas.q: Who are creditors?

children.note: Review the debtors list each week. A debt older than 30 days needs a call; stop new credit to customers who do not pay.
Count everything on the shelves and in the store at month-end, and value it at what you paid, not the selling price.
Use the buying price (or lower if damaged or expired). This follows the idea in IAS 2 Inventories and IFRS for SMEs.

manas.q: At what value do you count stock for your books?

children.note: Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases − closing stock. Without a count you cannot know your true profit.

manas.q: What is the formula for cost of goods sold?

children.note: If stock is lower than records say, you may have theft, damage, expiry or unrecorded drawings. Pharmacies should also check expiry dates.
Small businesses in Kenya mostly meet three taxes: turnover tax, normal income tax and VAT. Which applies depends on your sales. Rates change, so always check KRA.
A simple tax on gross sales for resident businesses with turnover above KES 1 million and not above KES 25 million a year. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: Which businesses fall under turnover tax?

children.note: TOT is 1.5% of gross sales from 1 July 2023 (Finance Act 2023). No expenses are deducted and it is a final tax. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the turnover tax rate?

children.note: File the TOT return and pay by the 20th of the month after the tax period, on iTax or the M-Service App (see the Filing on iTax map). (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Not for rental income, management, professional or training fees, income already taxed by final withholding tax, or non-residents. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
A business can leave TOT by giving KRA written notice, and then pays normal income tax on profit instead. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
If you are not on TOT (or opt out), you pay income tax on profit: sales minus allowable expenses. This needs fuller books (see the Filing on iTax map).
If your taxable sales reach KES 5 million or more in a year you must register for VAT. Below that, registration is voluntary under conditions. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: At what yearly sales must a Kenyan business register for VAT?

children.note: The general VAT rate is 16%. You pay output VAT on sales minus input VAT on purchases, by the 20th of the next month. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the general VAT rate in Kenya?

children.note: A TOT business whose vatable sales reach KES 5 million must also register for VAT. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
VAT-registered businesses must issue invoices through eTIMS. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

The Tax Procedures Act, section 23, says keep records in an official language (English or Kiswahili), in KES, for 5 years after the end of the period they relate to. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How long must a Kenyan business keep its records?

children.note: TOT: late filing KES 1,000 per month; late payment 5% plus interest of 1% per month. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What are the penalties for late turnover tax?

children.note: Real numbers in KES for a small Kenyan shop. Every figure below has been added up and checked.

children.topic: A Kibera duka's week of cash
children.note: Amina runs a duka in Kibera. Here is her cash book for one week, day by day.
Amina counts KES 4,000 in her Kibera duka box on Monday morning. All sales this week are in cash.
Start 4,000 + cash sales 6,200 − paid out 3,500 (stock (bread, milk) 3,500) = 6,700 in the box at night.
Start 6,700 + cash sales 5,800 − paid out 2,000 (stock (sugar, flour) 2,000) = 10,500 in the box at night.
Start 10,500 + cash sales 7,100 − paid out 4,400 (stock (soap, oil) 4,000, boda transport 400) = 13,200 in the box at night.
Start 13,200 + cash sales 6,500 − paid out 1,000 (electricity tokens 1,000) = 18,700 in the box at night.
Start 18,700 + cash sales 8,300 − paid out 5,500 (stock (soda, eggs) 5,500) = 21,500 in the box at night.
Start 21,500 + cash sales 9,400 − paid out 5,000 (helper wage 3,000, owner drawings 2,000) = 25,900 in the box at night.
Start 25,900 + cash sales 4,700 − paid out 10,000 (cash taken to the bank 10,000) = 20,600 in the box at night.
Opening 4,000 + receipts 48,000 − payments 31,400 = closing 20,600. It matches Sunday night's count, so the week balances.
The KES 2,000 on Saturday left the cash box, so it is in the cash book. But in the profit-and-loss it is drawings, not an expense.
On Saturday Amina takes KES 2,000 from the box for school fees. Dr Drawings 2,000 / Cr Cash 2,000. Debits equal credits.
Drawings reduce what the business owes the owner. Debit Drawings shows money taken out; credit Cash shows the box got smaller.
Amina takes soap that cost KES 300 for home use: Dr Drawings 300 / Cr Purchases 300. It is not a sale.

children.topic: A month's simple profit and loss
children.note: Amina's duka for October 2026, using her cash book, stock counts and receipts.
Sales 180,000. Cost of goods sold: opening stock 40,000 + purchases 120,000 − closing stock 35,000 = 125,000. Gross profit 180,000 − 125,000 = 55,000.
Expenses: rent 8,000, helper wages 12,000, electricity 1,500, transport 3,000, m-pesa and bank charges 700 = 25,200. Net profit 55,000 − 25,200 = 29,800.

children.topic: Drawings stay out of the P&L
children.note: Amina took 8,000 in drawings in October. It is not in the expenses, so profit stays 29,800.

Opening cash and M-Pesa 15,000 + money in 186,000 (sales 180,000 + a debtor paid 6,000) − money out 153,200 (purchases 120,000, expenses 25,200, drawings 8,000) = closing 47,800. Profit and cash differ because of stock, credit and drawings.

children.topic: Turnover tax for the month: KES 2,700
children.note: Gross sales 180,000 × 1.5% = 2,700. No expenses are deducted. Yearly sales of about 2,160,000 are within the TOT band and below the VAT line. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Float 5,000. Vouchers: milk for tea 600, cleaning 1,200, boda 850, photocopies 300, nails and tape 900 = 3,850. Cash left 1,150. 1,150 + 3,850 = 5,000, so top up 3,850.
Amina's list: Mama Wanjiku 1,800, Otieno (matatu crew) 2,500, Clinic next door 4,200. Total owed to her: KES 8,500.
A short, steady routine beats a big clean-up once a year. Learn the usual mistakes and test yourself.
Small jobs done daily, weekly and monthly (see the Month-end close map for the bigger version).
Write all sales and payments in the cash book, count the till, file receipts, and note credit sales and drawings.

manas.q: What should a small business owner do every day for the books?

children.note: Tick M-Pesa and bank statements against the book, top up petty cash, chase debtors, and check what you owe suppliers.

manas.q: What are the weekly bookkeeping jobs?

children.note: Count stock, prepare a simple P&L and cash summary, and file and pay tax by the 20th.

manas.q: What are the monthly bookkeeping jobs?

children.note: Add up the 12 months, file the yearly return, and store the year's records safely for at least 5 years.
These cause most of the trouble in small-business books.
Paying rent at home from the till without writing it down. Fix: separate accounts and record drawings.
This makes profit look smaller than it really is and gives wrong tax figures.
Without proof, KRA and lenders may not accept the cost. Always ask for a receipt or eTIMS invoice.
Transaction and withdrawal fees add up over a month. Record them from the statement.
Without it you cannot know cost of goods sold, so the profit figure is a guess.
A full box of cash may include money you owe suppliers. Profit and cash are different numbers.
Late returns and payments bring penalties and interest even when the tax is small.
A salon has gross sales of KES 95,000 in a month and is on TOT. What TOT is due?
TOT is on sales before any costs, so use KES 95,000.
95,000 × 1.5% = 1,425, due by the 20th of the next month. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Opening cash 3,000, money received 12,500, money paid 9,800. What should the till hold?
3,000 + 12,500 − 9,800 = 5,700. If the count is lower, record cash short and investigate.
A pharmacy: sales 60,000, cost of goods sold 38,000, expenses 9,500, drawings 5,000. Find net profit.
Drawings are not an expense, so ignore the 5,000.
